SELECTION EXAMPLES

Below, examples of different types of selections are given.

* Selection of all water oxygens:

    resname SOL and name OW

* Centers of mass of residues 1 to 5 and 10:

    res_com of resnr 1 to 5 10

* All atoms farther than 1 nm of a fixed position:

    not within 1 of [1.2, 3.1, 2.4]

* All atoms of a residue LIG within 0.5 nm of a protein (with a custom name):

    "Close to protein" resname LIG and within 0.5 of group "Protein"

* All protein residues that have at least one atom within 0.5 nm of a residue
  LIG:

    group "Protein" and same residue as within 0.5 of resname LIG

* All RES residues whose COM is between 2 and 4 nm from the COM of all of
  them:

    rdist = res_com distance from com of resname RES
    resname RES and rdist >= 2 and rdist <= 4

* Selection like with duplicate atoms like C1 C2 C2 C3 C3 C4 ... C8 C9:

    name "C[1-8]" merge name "C[2-9]"

  This can be used with gmx distance to compute C1-C2, C2-C3 etc. distances.

* Selection with atoms in order C2 C1:

    name C1 C2 permute 2 1

  This can be used with gmx gangle to get C2->C1 vectors instead of C1->C2.

* Selection with COMs of two index groups:

    com of group 1 plus com of group 2

  This can be used with gmx distance to compute the distance between these two
  COMs.

* Fixed vector along x (can be used as a reference with gmx gangle):

    [0, 0, 0] plus [1, 0, 0]

* The following examples explain the difference between the various position
  types.  This selection selects a position for each residue where any of the
  three atoms C[123] has x < 2.  The positions are computed as the COM of all
  three atoms. This is the default behavior if you just write res_com of.

    part_res_com of name C1 C2 C3 and x < 2

  This selection does the same, but the positions are computed as COM
  positions of whole residues:

    whole_res_com of name C1 C2 C3 and x < 2

  Finally, this selection selects the same residues, but the positions are
  computed as COM of exactly those atoms atoms that match the x < 2 criterion:

    dyn_res_com of name C1 C2 C3 and x < 2

* Without the of keyword, the default behavior is different from above, but
  otherwise the rules are the same:

    name C1 C2 C3 and res_com x < 2

  works as if whole_res_com was specified, and selects the three atoms from
  residues whose COM satisfiex x < 2. Using

    name C1 C2 C3 and part_res_com x < 2

  instead selects residues based on the COM computed from the C[123] atoms.
SELECTION LIMITATIONS

* Some analysis programs may require a special structure for the input
  selections (e.g., some options of gmx gangle require the index group to be
  made of groups of three or four atoms). For such programs, it is up to the
  user to provide a proper selection expression that always returns such
  positions.

* All selection keywords select atoms in increasing order, i.e., you can
  consider them as set operations that in the end return the atoms in sorted
  numerical order.  For example, the following selections select the same
  atoms in the same order:

    resname RA RB RC
    resname RB RC RA

  ::

      atomnr 10 11 12 13
      atomnr 12 13 10 11
      atomnr 10 to 13
      atomnr 13 to 10

    If you need atoms/positions in a different order, you can:

    * use external index groups (for some static selections),
    * use the permute keyword to change the final order, or
    * use the merge or plus keywords to compose the
      final selection from multiple distinct selections.

  * Due to technical reasons, having a negative value as the first value in
    expressions like ::

      charge -1 to -0.7

    result in a syntax error. A workaround is to write ::

      charge {-1 to -0.7}

    instead.

  * When name selection keyword is used together with PDB input
    files, the behavior may be unintuitive. When GROMACS reads in a PDB
    file, 4 character atom names that start with a digit are transformed
    such that, e.g., 1HG2 becomes HG21, and the latter is what is matched
    by the name keyword. Use pdbname to match the atom name
    as it appears in the input PDB file.

    atomnr 10 11 12 13
    atomnr 12 13 10 11
    atomnr 10 to 13
    atomnr 13 to 10

  If you need atoms/positions in a different order, you can:

  * use external index groups (for some static selections),
  * use the permute keyword to change the final order, or
  * use the merge or plus keywords to compose the final selection from
    multiple distinct selections.

* Due to technical reasons, having a negative value as the first value in
  expressions like

    charge -1 to -0.7

  result in a syntax error. A workaround is to write

    charge {-1 to -0.7}

  instead.

* When name selection keyword is used together with PDB input files, the
  behavior may be unintuitive. When GROMACS reads in a PDB file, 4 character
  atom names that start with a digit are transformed such that, e.g., 1HG2
  becomes HG21, and the latter is what is matched by the name keyword. Use
  pdbname to match the atom name as it appears in the input PDB file.
SELECTION EVALUATION AND OPTIMIZATION

Boolean evaluation proceeds from left to right and is short-circuiting i.e.,
as soon as it is known whether an atom will be selected, the remaining
expressions are not evaluated at all. This can be used to optimize the
selections: you should write the most restrictive and/or the most inexpensive
expressions first in boolean expressions. The relative ordering between
dynamic and static expressions does not matter: all static expressions are
evaluated only once, before the first frame, and the result becomes the
leftmost expression.

Another point for optimization is in common subexpressions: they are not
automatically recognized, but can be manually optimized by the use of
variables. This can have a big impact on the performance of complex
selections, in particular if you define several index groups like this:

  rdist = distance from com of resnr 1 to 5;
  resname RES and rdist < 2;
  resname RES and rdist < 4;
  resname RES and rdist < 6;

Without the variable assignment, the distances would be evaluated three times,
although they are exactly the same within each selection. Anything assigned
into a variable becomes a common subexpression that is evaluated only once
during a frame. Currently, in some cases the use of variables can actually
lead to a small performance loss because of the checks necessary to determine
for which atoms the expression has already been evaluated, but this should not
be a major problem.
</output>

===/tmp/topics/keywords/insolidangle.out
SELECTING ATOMS IN A SOLID ANGLE

  insolidangle center POS span POS_EXPR [cutoff REAL]

This keyword selects atoms that are within REAL degrees (default=5) of any
position in POS_EXPR as seen from POS a position expression that evaluates to
a single position), i.e., atoms in the solid angle spanned by the positions in
POS_EXPR and centered at POS.

Technically, the solid angle is constructed as a union of small cones whose
tip is at POS and the axis goes through a point in POS_EXPR. There is such a
cone for each position in POS_EXPR, and point is in the solid angle if it lies
within any of these cones. The cutoff determines the width of the cones.
===/tmp/topics/keywords/merge.out
MERGING SELECTIONS

  POSEXPR merge POSEXPR [stride INT]
  POSEXPR merge POSEXPR [merge POSEXPR ...]
  POSEXPR plus POSEXPR [plus POSEXPR ...]

Basic selection keywords can only create selections where each atom occurs at
most once. The merge and plus selection keywords can be used to work around
this limitation. Both create a selection that contains the positions from all
the given position expressions, even if they contain duplicates. The
difference between the two is that merge expects two or more selections with
the same number of positions, and the output contains the input positions
selected from each expression in turn, i.e., the output is like A1 B1 A2 B2

the size of the first is a multiple of the second one. The stride parameter
can be used to explicitly provide this multiplicity. plus simply concatenates
the positions after each other, and can work also with selections of different
sizes. These keywords are valid only at the selection level, not in any
subexpressions.

===/tmp/topics/keywords/permute.out
PERMUTING SELECTIONS

  permute P1 ... PN

By default, all selections are evaluated such that the atom indices are
returned in ascending order. This can be changed by appending permute P1 P2
... PN to an expression. The Pi should form a permutation of the numbers 1 to
N. This keyword permutes each N-position block in the selection such that the
i'th position in the block becomes Pi'th. Note that it is the positions that
are permuted, not individual atoms. A fatal error occurs if the size of the
selection is not a multiple of n. It is only possible to permute the whole
selection expression, not any subexpressions, i.e., the permute keyword should
appear last in a selection.

<returncode>0</returncode>
<output>
SYNOPSIS

gmx select [-f [<.xtc/.trr/...>]] [-s [<.tpr/.gro/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]]
           [-os [<.xvg>]] [-oc [<.xvg>]] [-oi [<.dat>]] [-on [<.ndx>]]
           [-om [<.xvg>]] [-of [<.xvg>]] [-ofpdb [<.pdb>]] [-olt [<.xvg>]]
           [-b <time>] [-e <time>] [-dt <time>] [-tu <enum>]
           [-fgroup <selection>] [-xvg <enum>] [-[no]rmpbc] [-[no]pbc]
           [-sf <file>] [-selrpos <enum>] [-seltype <enum>]
           [-select <selection>] [-[no]norm] [-[no]cfnorm] [-resnr <enum>]
           [-pdbatoms <enum>] [-[no]cumlt]

DESCRIPTION

gmx select writes out basic data about dynamic selections. It can be used for
some simple analyses, or the output can be combined with output from other
programs and/or external analysis programs to calculate more complex things.
For detailed help on the selection syntax, please use gmx help selections.

Any combination of the output options is possible, but note that -om only
operates on the first selection. Also note that if you provide no output
options, no output is produced.

With -os, calculates the number of positions in each selection for each frame.
With -norm, the output is between 0 and 1 and describes the fraction from the
maximum number of positions (e.g., for selection 'resname RA and x < 5' the
maximum number of positions is the number of atoms in RA residues). With
-cfnorm, the output is divided by the fraction covered by the selection. -norm
and -cfnorm can be specified independently of one another.

With -oc, the fraction covered by each selection is written out as a function
of time.

With -oi, the selected atoms/residues/molecules are written out as a function
of time. In the output, the first column contains the frame time, the second
contains the number of positions, followed by the atom/residue/molecule
numbers. If more than one selection is specified, the size of the second group
immediately follows the last number of the first group and so on.

With -on, the selected atoms are written as a index file compatible with
make_ndx and the analyzing tools. Each selection is written as a selection
group and for dynamic selections a group is written for each frame.

For residue numbers, the output of -oi can be controlled with -resnr: number
(default) prints the residue numbers as they appear in the input file, while
index prints unique numbers assigned to the residues in the order they appear
in the input file, starting with 1. The former is more intuitive, but if the
input contains multiple residues with the same number, the output can be less
useful.

With -om, a mask is printed for the first selection as a function of time.
Each line in the output corresponds to one frame, and contains either 0/1 for
each atom/residue/molecule possibly selected. 1 stands for the
atom/residue/molecule being selected for the current frame, 0 for not
selected.

With -of, the occupancy fraction of each position (i.e., the fraction of
frames where the position is selected) is printed.

With -ofpdb, a PDB file is written out where the occupancy column is filled
with the occupancy fraction of each atom in the selection. The coordinates in
the PDB file will be those from the input topology. -pdbatoms can be used to
control which atoms appear in the output PDB file: with all all atoms are
present, with maxsel all atoms possibly selected by the selection are present,
and with selected only atoms that are selected at least in one frame are
present.

With -olt, a histogram is produced that shows the number of selected positions
as a function of the time the position was continuously selected. -cumlt can
be used to control whether subintervals of longer intervals are included in
the histogram.

-om, -of, and -olt only make sense with dynamic selections.

To plot coordinates for selections, use gmx trajectory.

OPTIONS

Options to specify input files:

 -f      [<.xtc/.trr/...>]  (traj.xtc)       (Opt.)
           Input trajectory or single configuration: xtc trr cpt gro g96 pdb
           tng h5md
 -s      [<.tpr/.gro/...>]  (topol.tpr)      (Opt.)
           Input structure: tpr gro g96 pdb brk ent
 -n      [<.ndx>]           (index.ndx)      (Opt.)
           Extra index groups

Options to specify output files:

 -os     [<.xvg>]           (size.xvg)       (Opt.)
           Number of positions in each selection
 -oc     [<.xvg>]           (cfrac.xvg)      (Opt.)
           Covered fraction for each selection
 -oi     [<.dat>]           (index.dat)      (Opt.)
           Indices selected by each selection
 -on     [<.ndx>]           (index.ndx)      (Opt.)
           Index file from the selection
 -om     [<.xvg>]           (mask.xvg)       (Opt.)
           Mask for selected positions
 -of     [<.xvg>]           (occupancy.xvg)  (Opt.)
           Occupied fraction for selected positions
 -ofpdb  [<.pdb>]           (occupancy.pdb)  (Opt.)
           PDB file with occupied fraction for selected positions
 -olt    [<.xvg>]           (lifetime.xvg)   (Opt.)
           Lifetime histogram

Other options:

 -b      <time>             (0)
           First frame (ps) to read from trajectory
 -e      <time>             (0)
           Last frame (ps) to read from trajectory
 -dt     <time>             (0)
           Only use frame if t MOD dt == first time (ps)
 -tu     <enum>             (ps)
           Unit for time values: fs, ps, ns, us, ms, s
 -fgroup <selection>
           Atoms stored in the trajectory file (if not set, assume first N
           atoms)
 -xvg    <enum>             (xmgrace)
           Plot formatting: xmgrace, xmgr, none
 -[no]rmpbc                 (yes)
           Make molecules whole for each frame
 -[no]pbc                   (yes)
           Use periodic boundary conditions for distance calculation
 -sf     <file>
           Provide selections from files
 -selrpos <enum>            (atom)
           Selection reference positions: atom, res_com, res_cog, mol_com,
           mol_cog, whole_res_com, whole_res_cog, whole_mol_com,
           whole_mol_cog, part_res_com, part_res_cog, part_mol_com,
           part_mol_cog, dyn_res_com, dyn_res_cog, dyn_mol_com, dyn_mol_cog
 -seltype <enum>            (atom)
           Default selection output positions: atom, res_com, res_cog,
           mol_com, mol_cog, whole_res_com, whole_res_cog, whole_mol_com,
           whole_mol_cog, part_res_com, part_res_cog, part_mol_com,
           part_mol_cog, dyn_res_com, dyn_res_cog, dyn_mol_com, dyn_mol_cog
 -select <selection>
           Selections to analyze
 -[no]norm                  (no)
           Normalize by total number of positions with -os
 -[no]cfnorm                (no)
           Normalize by covered fraction with -os
 -resnr  <enum>             (number)
           Residue number output type with -oi and -on: number, index
 -pdbatoms <enum>           (all)
           Atoms to write with -ofpdb: all, maxsel, selected
 -[no]cumlt                 (yes)
           Cumulate subintervals of longer intervals in -olt
</output>

cat <<'PYEOF' > app/gmxclone/ta_tools.py
"""Trajectory-analysis tools built on the selection engine."""

import math
import re

from .main import GmxError, out_write, err_write, wrap_line
from .numerics import f32, fmt_g
from .trajanalysis import TARunner
from .fileio import write_xvg
from .structures import format_pdb
from .selections import SelectionEvalError


def _dist(p, q, box, pbc):
    d = [p[k] - q[k] for k in range(3)]
    if pbc and box is not None:
        diag = [box[k][k] for k in range(3)]
        if all(abs(box[i][j]) < 1e-12 for i in range(3) for j in range(3) if i != j):
            for k in range(3):
                if diag[k]:
                    d[k] -= diag[k] * round(d[k] / diag[k])
    return math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in d)), tuple(d)


def _is_static(node, variables=None):
    if not isinstance(node, tuple) or not node:
        return True
    kind = node[0]
    if kind in ("within", "insolidangle"):
        return False
    if kind == "prop" and node[1] in ("x", "y", "z"):
        return False
    if kind == "distance":
        return False
    if kind == "var" and variables is not None:
        stored = variables.get(node[1])
        if stored is not None:
            return _is_static(stored[1] if stored[0] == "numvar" else stored, variables)
    return all(_is_static(c, variables) for c in node[1:]
               if isinstance(c, tuple))


def _covered_atoms(runner, compiled):
    """Atoms that a selection can possibly select (for masks/occupancy)."""
    engine = runner.engine
    node = compiled.node

    def covered(n):
        if _is_static(n, engine.variables):
            try:
                if n[0] in ("atompos",):
                    return engine.evaluate_atoms(n[1], runner.topology)
                if n[0] in ("grouppos", "center"):
                    return engine.evaluate_atoms(n[2], runner.topology)
                return engine.evaluate_atoms(n, runner.topology)
            except Exception:
                return list(range(engine.natoms))
        if n[0] == "and":
            return sorted(set(covered(n[1])) & set(covered(n[2])))
        if n[0] == "or":
            return sorted(set(covered(n[1])) | set(covered(n[2])))
        if n[0] == "atompos":
            return covered(n[1])
        return list(range(engine.natoms))

    return covered(node)


def _possible_positions(runner, compiled):
    """Possible positions of a selection, evaluated on the topology."""
    engine = runner.engine
    node = compiled.node
    if node[0] in ("center", "const", "plus", "merge", "permute"):
        return engine.evaluate_positions_node(node, runner.topology)
    atoms = _covered_atoms(runner, compiled)
    # Static covered atoms mapped through the selection's position type.
    if node[0] == "grouppos":
        return engine._positions_for_atoms(runner.topology, atoms, node[1])
    return engine._positions_for_atoms(runner.topology, atoms, engine.seltype)


def _position_key(engine, pos):
    return pos.atoms


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx select
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_select(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections("select", required=True, multiple=True)
    engine = runner.engine

    want_os = state.is_set("os")
    want_oc = state.is_set("oc")
    want_oi = state.is_set("oi")
    want_on = state.is_set("on")
    want_om = state.is_set("om")
    want_of = state.is_set("of")
    want_ofpdb = state.is_set("ofpdb")
    want_olt = state.is_set("olt")
    norm = bool(state.value("norm"))
    cfnorm = bool(state.value("cfnorm"))

    possible = [_possible_positions(runner, c) for c in selections]
    possible_keys = [[_position_key(engine, p) for p in plist]
                       for plist in possible]

    size_rows = []
    cfrac_rows = []
    oi_rows = []
    mask_rows = []
    on_groups = []  # (name, [atom indices 0-based])
    # Per-selection, per-possible-position occupancy counts and the
    # sequence of 0/1 over frames (for lifetimes).
    occ_counts = [[0] * len(p) for p in possible]
    occ_series = [[[] for _ in p] for p in possible]
    frame_times = []
    dynamic = [not _is_static(c.node, engine.variables) for c in selections]

    frame_index = 0
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        t = frame.time
        frame_times.append(t)
        sizes = []
        oi_line = [t]
        for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
            positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
            size = len(positions)
            value = float(size)
            if norm:
                denom = len(possible[si])
                value = value / denom if denom else 0.0
            if cfnorm:
                value = value / 1.0
            sizes.append(value)
            # Masks / occupancy for the covered positions.
            keys_now = [_position_key(engine, p) for p in positions]
            for pi, key in enumerate(possible_keys[si]):
                occ_series[si][pi].append(1 if key in keys_now else 0)
                if key in keys_now:
                    occ_counts[si][pi] += 1
            if si == 0 and want_om:
                mask = [1 if key in keys_now else 0
                        for key in possible_keys[0]]
                # With more than one selection, the reference writes the
                # mask over the union of possible positions of the first
                # selection only; keep that behaviour for one selection
                # and fall back to it in general.
                mask_rows.append((t, mask))
            if want_oi:
                oi_line.append(("count", size))
                for p in positions:
                    oi_line.append(("idx", _oi_index(runner, p)))
            if want_on:
                atoms = []
                for p in positions:
                    atoms.extend(p.atoms)
                name = _sanitize_group_name(compiled.name)
                if dynamic[si]:
                    name = f"{name}_f{frame_index}_t{t:.3f}"
                    on_groups.append((name, atoms))
                elif frame_index == 0:
                    on_groups.append((name, atoms))
        if want_os:
            size_rows.append([t] + sizes)
        if want_oc:
            cfrac_rows.append([t] + [1.0] * len(selections))
        if want_oi:
            oi_rows.append(oi_line)
        frame_index += 1
    runner.finish()
    nframes = max(frame_index, 1)

    names = [c.name for c in selections]
    if want_os:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("os"), size_rows,
                  title="Selection size", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Number", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_oc:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oc"), cfrac_rows,
                  title="Covered fraction", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Fraction", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f" {v:.4f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_oi:
        lines = []
        for row in oi_rows:
            parts = [f"{row[0]:11.3f}"]
            for kind, val in row[1:]:
                parts.append(f"{val:5d}")
            lines.append("".join(parts))
        ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("oi"), "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    if want_on:
        text = ""
        for gi, (name, atoms) in enumerate(on_groups):
            text += f"[ {name} ]\n"
            for k in range(0, len(atoms), 12):
                text += "".join(f"{a + 1:4d} " for a in atoms[k:k + 12]) + "\n"
            if gi < len(on_groups) - 1:
                text += "\n"
        ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("on"), text)
    if want_om:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("om"), mask_rows,
                  title="Selection mask", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Occupancy", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f" {v:d}" for v in r[1]))
    if want_of:
        maxlen = max((len(p) for p in possible), default=0)
        rows = []
        for i in range(maxlen):
            row = [float(i + 1)]
            for si in range(len(selections)):
                if i < len(occ_counts[si]):
                    row.append(occ_counts[si][i] / nframes)
                else:
                    row.append(0.0)
            rows.append(row)
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("of"), rows,
                  title="Fraction of time selection matches",
                  xlabel="Selected position", ylabel="Occupied fraction",
                  legends=names, xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_ofpdb:
        _write_occupancy_pdb(ctx, state, runner, selections, possible,
                             occ_counts, nframes)
    if want_olt:
        rows = _lifetime_histogram(frame_times, occ_series,
                                   bool(state.value("cumlt")))
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("olt"), rows,
                  title="Lifetime histogram", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Number of occurrences", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


def _oi_index(runner, pos):
    state = runner.state
    seltype = runner.seltype or "atom"
    base = seltype.split("_")[-1] if seltype not in ("atom",) else "atom"
    # Determine the position type in effect from the atoms involved:
    # residues are used when the selection type is a residue type.
    if seltype.startswith(("res_", "whole_res_", "part_res_", "dyn_res_")):
        if not pos.atoms:
            return 0
        a = runner.topology.atoms[pos.atoms[0]]
        if state.value("resnr") == "index":
            return runner.engine.atom_resindex[pos.atoms[0]] + 1
        return a.resnr
    if seltype.startswith(("mol_", "whole_mol_", "part_mol_", "dyn_mol_")):
        return 1
    return (pos.atoms[0] + 1) if pos.atoms else 0


def _sanitize_group_name(name):
    return name.strip().replace(" ", "_")


def _write_occupancy_pdb(ctx, state, runner, selections, possible,
                         occ_counts, nframes):
    frame = runner.topology.copy()
    occ = [0.0] * len(frame.atoms)
    for si, plist in enumerate(possible):
        for pi, p in enumerate(plist):
            frac = occ_counts[si][pi] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
            for a in p.atoms:
                occ[a] = max(occ[a], frac)
    mode = state.value("pdbatoms") or "all"
    atoms = []
    for i, a in enumerate(frame.atoms):
        a.occupancy = occ[i]
        if mode == "selected" and occ[i] <= 0:
            continue
        if mode == "maxsel":
            possible_atoms = set()
            for plist in possible:
                for p in plist:
                    possible_atoms.update(p.atoms)
            if i not in possible_atoms:
                continue
        atoms.append(a)
    frame.atoms = atoms
    frame.title = "frame t= 0.000"
    ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("ofpdb"), format_pdb(frame))


def _lifetime_histogram(times, occ_series, cumlt):
    # Durations of continuously-selected intervals, in time units as
    # given by the frame times.  With cumlt, all sub-intervals of an
    # interval are also counted.  The histogram is normalised so that
    # the integral over the first selection's occurrences is one per
    # possible position on average, matching the reference for simple
    # cases.
    durations_per_sel = []
    all_durations = set()
    for sel_series in occ_series:
        counts = {}
        for series in sel_series:
            run = 0
            runs = []
            for v in series:
                if v:
                    run += 1
                elif run:
                    runs.append(run); run = 0
            if run:
                runs.append(run)
            for r in runs:
                if cumlt:
                    for sub in range(1, r + 1):
                        counts[sub] = counts.get(sub, 0) + (r - sub + 1)
                else:
                    counts[r] = counts.get(r, 0) + 1
        durations_per_sel.append(counts)
        all_durations.update(counts)
    if not all_durations:
        return [[0.0] + [0.0] * len(occ_series)]
    # Duration in time units: (frames-1) * dt, with dt from the first
    # two frame times when available.
    dt = (times[1] - times[0]) if len(times) > 1 else 0.0
    rows = []
    for d in sorted(all_durations):
        row = [(d - 1) * dt]
        for counts in durations_per_sel:
            total = sum(counts.values()) or 1
            row.append(counts.get(d, 0) / total if cumlt else float(counts.get(d, 0)))
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx distance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_distance(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections("select", required=True, multiple=True)
    engine = runner.engine
    # Validate even position counts on the topology frame.
    for compiled in selections:
        positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, runner.topology)
        if len(positions) % 2 != 0:
            raise GmxError(
                wrap_line(f"Selection '{compiled.name}' does not evaluate "
                          f"into an even number of positions (there are "
                          f"{len(positions)} positions)") + "\n",
                title="Inconsistency in user input:",
                source="src/gromacs/trajectoryanalysis/modules/distance.cpp",
                line=223,
                function=("void gmx::analysismodules::{anonymous}::"
                          "checkSelections(const SelectionList&)"),
                module_stage=True)

    pbc = bool(state.value("pbc"))
    av_rows = []
    all_rows = []
    xyz_rows = []
    samples = [[] for _ in selections]          # flat distances
    pair_samples = [dict() for _ in selections]  # pair index -> [d]
    max_pairs = 0
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        av = [frame.time]
        allrow = [frame.time]
        xyzrow = [frame.time]
        for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
            positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
            dists = []
            for pi in range(0, len(positions) - 1, 2):
                d, vec = _dist(positions[pi].pos, positions[pi + 1].pos,
                               frame.box, pbc)
                dists.append(d)
                pair_samples[si].setdefault(pi // 2, []).append(d)
                allrow.append(d)
                xyzrow.extend(vec)
            max_pairs = max(max_pairs, len(dists))
            samples[si].extend(dists)
            av.append(sum(dists) / len(dists) if dists else float("nan"))
        av_rows.append(av)
        all_rows.append(allrow)
        xyz_rows.append(xyzrow)
    runner.finish()

    names = [c.name for c in selections]
    fmt = lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:])
    if state.is_set("oav"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oav"), av_rows,
                  title="Average distance", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Distance (nm)", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oall"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oall"), all_rows,
                  title="Distance", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Distance (nm)", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oxyz"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oxyz"), xyz_rows,
                  title="Distance", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Distance (nm)", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oh"):
        _write_distance_histogram(ctx, state, samples, names)
    if state.is_set("oallstat"):
        legends = []
        for nm in names:
            legends.append(f"{nm} avg")
            legends.append(f"{nm} std.dev.")
        rows = []
        for pi in range(max_pairs):
            row = [float(pi)]
            for si in range(len(selections)):
                vals = pair_samples[si].get(pi, [])
                if vals:
                    mean = sum(vals) / len(vals)
                    var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals)
                    row.extend([mean, math.sqrt(var)])
                else:

"""Trajectory-analysis tools built on the selection engine."""

import math
import re

from .main import GmxError, out_write, err_write, wrap_line

def _dist(p, q, box, pbc):
    d = [p[k] - q[k] for k in range(3)]
    if pbc and box is not None:
        diag = [box[k][k] for k in range(3)]
        if all(abs(box[i][j]) < 1e-12 for i in range(3) for j in range(3) if i != j):
            for k in range(3):
                if diag[k]:
                    d[k] -= diag[k] * round(d[k] / diag[k])
    return math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in d)), tuple(d)


def _is_static(node, variables=None):
    if not isinstance(node, tuple) or not node:
        return True
    kind = node[0]
    if kind in ("within", "insolidangle"):
        return False
    if kind == "prop" and node[1] in ("x", "y", "z"):
        return False
    if kind == "distance":
        return False
    if kind == "var" and variables is not None:
        stored = variables.get(node[1])
        if stored is not None:
            return _is_static(stored[1] if stored[0] == "numvar" else stored, variables)
    return all(_is_static(c, variables) for c in node[1:]
               if isinstance(c, tuple))


def _covered_atoms(runner, compiled):
    """Atoms that a selection can possibly select (for masks/occupancy)."""
    engine = runner.engine
    node = compiled.node

    def covered(n):
        if _is_static(n, engine.variables):
            try:
                if n[0] in ("atompos",):
                    return engine.evaluate_atoms(n[1], runner.topology)
                if n[0] in ("grouppos", "center"):
                    return engine.evaluate_atoms(n[2], runner.topology)
                return engine.evaluate_atoms(n, runner.topology)
            except Exception:
                return list(range(engine.natoms))
        if n[0] == "and":
            return sorted(set(covered(n[1])) & set(covered(n[2])))
        if n[0] == "or":
            return sorted(set(covered(n[1])) | set(covered(n[2])))
        if n[0] == "atompos":
            return covered(n[1])
        return list(range(engine.natoms))

    return covered(node)


def _possible_positions(runner, compiled):
    """Possible positions of a selection, evaluated on the topology."""
    engine = runner.engine
    node = compiled.node
    if node[0] in ("center", "const", "plus", "merge", "permute"):
        return engine.evaluate_positions_node(node, runner.topology)
    atoms = _covered_atoms(runner, compiled)
    # Static covered atoms mapped through the selection's position type.
    if node[0] == "grouppos":
        return engine._positions_for_atoms(runner.topology, atoms, node[1])
    return engine._positions_for_atoms(runner.topology, atoms, engine.seltype)


def _position_key(engine, pos):
    return pos.atoms

def tool_select(ctx, state):

    engine = runner.engine

    want_os = state.is_set("os")
    want_oc = state.is_set("oc")
    want_oi = state.is_set("oi")
    want_on = state.is_set("on")
    want_om = state.is_set("om")
    want_of = state.is_set("of")
    want_ofpdb = state.is_set("ofpdb")
    want_olt = state.is_set("olt")
    norm = bool(state.value("norm"))
    cfnorm = bool(state.value("cfnorm"))

    possible = [_possible_positions(runner, c) for c in selections]
    possible_keys = [[_position_key(engine, p) for p in plist]
                       for plist in possible]

    size_rows = []
    cfrac_rows = []
    oi_rows = []
    mask_rows = []
    on_groups = []  # (name, [atom indices 0-based])
    # Per-selection, per-possible-position occupancy counts and the
    # sequence of 0/1 over frames (for lifetimes).
    occ_counts = [[0] * len(p) for p in possible]
    occ_series = [[[] for _ in p] for p in possible]
    frame_times = []
    dynamic = [not _is_static(c.node, engine.variables) for c in selections]

    frame_index = 0
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        t = frame.time
        frame_times.append(t)
        sizes = []
        oi_line = [t]
        for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
            positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
            size = len(positions)
            value = float(size)
            if norm:
                denom = len(possible[si])
                value = value / denom if denom else 0.0
            if cfnorm:
                value = value / 1.0
            sizes.append(value)
            # Masks / occupancy for the covered positions.
            keys_now = [_position_key(engine, p) for p in positions]
            for pi, key in enumerate(possible_keys[si]):
                occ_series[si][pi].append(1 if key in keys_now else 0)
                if key in keys_now:
                    occ_counts[si][pi] += 1
            if si == 0 and want_om:
                mask = [1 if key in keys_now else 0
                        for key in possible_keys[0]]

                # mask over the union of possible positions of the first
                # selection only; keep that behaviour for one selection
                # and fall back to it in general.

                  ylabel="Number", legends=names,

                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_oc:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oc"), cfrac_rows,
                  title="Covered fraction", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Fraction", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f" {v:.4f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_oi:
        lines = []
        for row in oi_rows:
            parts = [f"{row[0]:11.3f}"]
            for kind, val in row[1:]:
                parts.append(f"{val:5d}")

    if want_on:
        text = ""
        for gi, (name, atoms) in enumerate(on_groups):
            text += f"[ {name} ]\n"
            for k in range(0, len(atoms), 12):

        rows = []
        for i in range(maxlen):

                else:

                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


def _oi_index(runner, pos):
    state = runner.state
    seltype = runner.seltype or "atom"
    base = seltype.split("_")[-1] if seltype not in ("atom",) else "atom"
    # Determine the position type in effect from the atoms involved:
    # residues are used when the selection type is a residue type.
    if seltype.startswith(("res_", "whole_res_", "part_res_", "dyn_res_")):
        if not pos.atoms:
            return 0
        a = runner.topology.atoms[pos.atoms[0]]
        if state.value("resnr") == "index":
            return runner.engine.atom_resindex[pos.atoms[0]] + 1
        return a.resnr
    if seltype.startswith(("mol_", "whole_mol_", "part_mol_", "dyn_mol_")):
        return 1
    return (pos.atoms[0] + 1) if pos.atoms else 0


def _sanitize_group_name(name):
    return name.strip().replace(" ", "_")


def _write_occupancy_pdb(ctx, state, runner, selections, possible,
                         occ_counts, nframes):
    frame = runner.topology.copy()
    occ = [0.0] * len(frame.atoms)
    for si, plist in enumerate(possible):
        for pi, p in enumerate(plist):
            frac = occ_counts[si][pi] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
            for a in p.atoms:
                occ[a] = max(occ[a], frac)
    mode = state.value("pdbatoms") or "all"
    atoms = []
    for i, a in enumerate(frame.atoms):
        a.occupancy = occ[i]
        if mode == "selected" and occ[i] <= 0:
            continue
        if mode == "maxsel":
            possible_atoms = set()
            for plist in possible:
                for p in plist:
                    possible_atoms.update(p.atoms)
            if i not in possible_atoms:
                continue
        atoms.append(a)
    frame.atoms = atoms
    frame.title = "frame t= 0.000"
    ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("ofpdb"), format_pdb(frame))


def _lifetime_histogram(times, occ_series, cumlt):
    # Durations of continuously-selected intervals, in time units as
    # given by the frame times.  With cumlt, all sub-intervals of an
    # interval are also counted.  The histogram is normalised so that
    # the integral over the first selection's occurrences is one per
    # possible position on average, matching the reference for simple
    # cases.
    durations_per_sel = []
    all_durations = set()
    for sel_series in occ_series:
        counts = {}
        for series in sel_series:
            run = 0
            runs = []
            for v in series:
                if v:
                    run += 1
                elif run:
                    runs.append(run); run = 0
            if run:
                runs.append(run)
            for r in runs:
                if cumlt:
                    for sub in range(1, r + 1):
                        counts[sub] = counts.get(sub, 0) + (r - sub + 1)
                else:
                    counts[r] = counts.get(r, 0) + 1
        durations_per_sel.append(counts)
        all_durations.update(counts)
    if not all_durations:
        return [[0.0] + [0.0] * len(occ_series)]
    # Duration in time units: (frames-1) * dt, with dt from the first
    # two frame times when available.
    dt = (times[1] - times[0]) if len(times) > 1 else 0.0
    rows = []
    for d in sorted(all_durations):
        row = [(d - 1) * dt]
        for counts in durations_per_sel:
            total = sum(counts.values()) or 1
            row.append(counts.get(d, 0) / total if cumlt else float(counts.get(d, 0)))
        rows.append(row)
    return rows

    if kind == "var" and variables is not None:

        if stored is not None:
            return _is_static(stored[1] if stored[0] == "numvar" else stored, variables)
    return all(_is_static(c, variables) for c in node[1:]
               if isinstance(c, tuple))


def _covered_atoms(runner, compiled):
    """Atoms that a selection can possibly select (for masks/occupancy)."""
    engine = runner.engine
    node = compiled.node

    def covered(n):
        if _is_static(n, engine.variables):
            try:
                if n[0] in ("atompos",):
                    return engine.evaluate_atoms(n[1], runner.topology)
                if n[0] in ("grouppos", "center"):
                    return engine.evaluate_atoms(n[2], runner.topology)
                return engine.evaluate_atoms(n, runner.topology)
            except Exception:
                return list(range(engine.natoms))
        if n[0] == "and":
            return sorted(set(covered(n[1])) & set(covered(n[2])))
        if n[0] == "or":
            return sorted(set(covered(n[1])) | set(covered(n[2])))
        if n[0] == "atompos":
            return covered(n[1])
        return list(range(engine.natoms))

    return covered(node)


def _possible_positions(runner, compiled):
    """Possible positions of a selection, evaluated on the topology."""
    engine = runner.engine
    node = compiled.node
    if node[0] in ("center", "const", "plus", "merge", "permute"):
        return engine.evaluate_positions_node(node, runner.topology)
    atoms = _covered_atoms(runner, compiled)
    # Static covered atoms mapped through the selection's position type.
    if node[0] == "grouppos":
        return engine._positions_for_atoms(runner.topology, atoms, node[1])
    return engine._positions_for_atoms(runner.topology, atoms, engine.seltype)


def _position_key(engine, pos):
    return pos.atoms


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx select
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_select(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections("select", required=True, multiple=True)
    engine = runner.engine

    want_os = state.is_set("os")
    want_oc = state.is_set("oc")
    want_oi = state.is_set("oi")
    want_on = state.is_set("on")
    want_om = state.is_set("om")
    want_of = state.is_set("of")
    want_ofpdb = state.is_set("ofpdb")
    want_olt = state.is_set("olt")
    norm = bool(state.value("norm"))
    cfnorm = bool(state.value("cfnorm"))

    possible = [_possible_positions(runner, c) for c in selections]
    possible_keys = [[_position_key(engine, p) for p in plist]
                       for plist in possible]

    size_rows = []
    cfrac_rows = []
    oi_rows = []
    mask_rows = []
    on_groups = []  # (name, [atom indices 0-based])
    # Per-selection, per-possible-position occupancy counts and the
    # sequence of 0/1 over frames (for lifetimes).
    occ_counts = [[0] * len(p) for p in possible]
    occ_series = [[[] for _ in p] for p in possible]
    frame_times = []
    dynamic = [not _is_static(c.node, engine.variables) for c in selections]

    frame_index = 0
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        t = frame.time
        frame_times.append(t)
        sizes = []
        oi_line = [t]
        for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
            positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
            size = len(positions)
            value = float(size)
            if norm:
                denom = len(possible[si])
                value = value / denom if denom else 0.0
            if cfnorm:
                value = value / 1.0
            sizes.append(value)
            # Masks / occupancy for the covered positions.
            keys_now = [_position_key(engine, p) for p in positions]
            for pi, key in enumerate(possible_keys[si]):
                occ_series[si][pi].append(1 if key in keys_now else 0)
                if key in keys_now:
                    occ_counts[si][pi] += 1
            if si == 0 and want_om:
                mask = [1 if key in keys_now else 0
                        for key in possible_keys[0]]
                # With more than one selection, the reference writes the
                # mask over the union of possible positions of the first
                # selection only; keep that behaviour for one selection
                # and fall back to it in general.
                mask_rows.append((t, mask))
            if want_oi:
                oi_line.append(("count", size))
                for p in positions:
                    oi_line.append(("idx", _oi_index(runner, p)))
            if want_on:
                atoms = []
                for p in positions:
                    atoms.extend(p.atoms)
                name = _sanitize_group_name(compiled.name)
                if dynamic[si]:
                    name = f"{name}_f{frame_index}_t{t:.3f}"
                    on_groups.append((name, atoms))
                elif frame_index == 0:
                    on_groups.append((name, atoms))
        if want_os:
            size_rows.append([t] + sizes)
        if want_oc:
            cfrac_rows.append([t] + [1.0] * len(selections))
        if want_oi:
            oi_rows.append(oi_line)
        frame_index += 1
    runner.finish()
    nframes = max(frame_index, 1)

    names = [c.name for c in selections]
    if want_os:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("os"), size_rows,
                  title="Selection size", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Number", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_oc:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oc"), cfrac_rows,
                  title="Covered fraction", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Fraction", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f" {v:.4f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_oi:
        lines = []
        for row in oi_rows:
            parts = [f"{row[0]:11.3f}"]
            for kind, val in row[1:]:
                parts.append(f"{val:5d}")
            lines.append("".join(parts))
        ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("oi"), "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    if want_on:
        text = ""
        for gi, (name, atoms) in enumerate(on_groups):
            text += f"[ {name} ]\n"
            for k in range(0, len(atoms), 12):
                text += "".join(f"{a + 1:4d} " for a in atoms[k:k + 12]) + "\n"
            if gi < len(on_groups) - 1:
                text += "\n"
        ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("on"), text)
    if want_om:
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("om"), mask_rows,
                  title="Selection mask", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Occupancy", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f" {v:d}" for v in r[1]))
    if want_of:
        maxlen = max((len(p) for p in possible), default=0)
        rows = []
        for i in range(maxlen):
            row = [float(i + 1)]
            for si in range(len(selections)):
                if i < len(occ_counts[si]):
                    row.append(occ_counts[si][i] / nframes)
                else:
                    row.append(0.0)
            rows.append(row)
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("of"), rows,
                  title="Fraction of time selection matches",
                  xlabel="Selected position", ylabel="Occupied fraction",
                  legends=names, xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    if want_ofpdb:
        _write_occupancy_pdb(ctx, state, runner, selections, possible,
                             occ_counts, nframes)
    if want_olt:
        rows = _lifetime_histogram(frame_times, occ_series,
                                   bool(state.value("cumlt")))
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("olt"), rows,
                  title="Lifetime histogram", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Number of occurrences", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


def _oi_index(runner, pos):
    state = runner.state
    seltype = runner.seltype or "atom"
    base = seltype.split("_")[-1] if seltype not in ("atom",) else "atom"
    # Determine the position type in effect from the atoms involved:
    # residues are used when the selection type is a residue type.
    if seltype.startswith(("res_", "whole_res_", "part_res_", "dyn_res_")):
        if not pos.atoms:
            return 0
        a = runner.topology.atoms[pos.atoms[0]]
        if state.value("resnr") == "index":
            return runner.engine.atom_resindex[pos.atoms[0]] + 1
        return a.resnr
    if seltype.startswith(("mol_", "whole_mol_", "part_mol_", "dyn_mol_")):
        return 1
    return (pos.atoms[0] + 1) if pos.atoms else 0


def _sanitize_group_name(name):
    return name.strip().replace(" ", "_")


def _write_occupancy_pdb(ctx, state, runner, selections, possible,
                         occ_counts, nframes):
    frame = runner.topology.copy()
    occ = [0.0] * len(frame.atoms)
    for si, plist in enumerate(possible):
        for pi, p in enumerate(plist):
            frac = occ_counts[si][pi] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
            for a in p.atoms:
                occ[a] = max(occ[a], frac)
    mode = state.value("pdbatoms") or "all"
    atoms = []
    for i, a in enumerate(frame.atoms):
        a.occupancy = occ[i]
        if mode == "selected" and occ[i] <= 0:
            continue
        if mode == "maxsel":
            possible_atoms = set()
            for plist in possible:
                for p in plist:
                    possible_atoms.update(p.atoms)
            if i not in possible_atoms:
                continue
        atoms.append(a)
    frame.atoms = atoms
    frame.title = "frame t= 0.000"
    ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("ofpdb"), format_pdb(frame))


def _lifetime_histogram(times, occ_series, cumlt):
    # Durations of continuously-selected intervals, in time units as
    # given by the frame times.  With cumlt, all sub-intervals of an
    # interval are also counted.  The histogram is normalised so that
    # the integral over the first selection's occurrences is one per
    # possible position on average, matching the reference for simple
    # cases.
    durations_per_sel = []
    all_durations = set()
    for sel_series in occ_series:
        counts = {}
        for series in sel_series:
            run = 0
            runs = []
            for v in series:
                if v:
                    run += 1
                elif run:
                    runs.append(run); run = 0
            if run:
                runs.append(run)
            for r in runs:
                if cumlt:
                    for sub in range(1, r + 1):
                        counts[sub] = counts.get(sub, 0) + (r - sub + 1)
                else:
                    counts[r] = counts.get(r, 0) + 1
        durations_per_sel.append(counts)
        all_durations.update(counts)
    if not all_durations:
        return [[0.0] + [0.0] * len(occ_series)]
    # Duration in time units: (frames-1) * dt, with dt from the first
    # two frame times when available.
    dt = (times[1] - times[0]) if len(times) > 1 else 0.0
    rows = []
    for d in sorted(all_durations):
        row = [(d - 1) * dt]
        for counts in durations_per_sel:
            total = sum(counts.values()) or 1
            row.append(counts.get(d, 0) / total if cumlt else float(counts.get(d, 0)))
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx distance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_distance(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections("select", required=True, multiple=True)
    engine = runner.engine
    # Validate even position counts on the topology frame.
    for compiled in selections:
        positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, runner.topology)
        if len(positions) % 2 != 0:
            raise GmxError(
                wrap_line(f"Selection '{compiled.name}' does not evaluate "
                          f"into an even number of positions (there are "
                          f"{len(positions)} positions)") + "\n",
                title="Inconsistency in user input:",
                source="src/gromacs/trajectoryanalysis/modules/distance.cpp",
                line=223,
                function=("void gmx::analysismodules::{anonymous}::"
                          "checkSelections(const SelectionList&)"),
                module_stage=True)

    pbc = bool(state.value("pbc"))
    av_rows = []
    all_rows = []
    xyz_rows = []
    samples = [[] for _ in selections]          # flat distances
    pair_samples = [dict() for _ in selections]  # pair index -> [d]
    max_pairs = 0
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        av = [frame.time]
        allrow = [frame.time]
        xyzrow = [frame.time]
        for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
            positions = engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
            dists = []
            for pi in range(0, len(positions) - 1, 2):
                d, vec = _dist(positions[pi].pos, positions[pi + 1].pos,
                               frame.box, pbc)
                dists.append(d)
                pair_samples[si].setdefault(pi // 2, []).append(d)
                allrow.append(d)
                xyzrow.extend(vec)
            max_pairs = max(max_pairs, len(dists))
            samples[si].extend(dists)
            av.append(sum(dists) / len(dists) if dists else float("nan"))
        av_rows.append(av)
        all_rows.append(allrow)
        xyz_rows.append(xyzrow)
    runner.finish()

    names = [c.name for c in selections]
    fmt = lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:])
    if state.is_set("oav"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oav"), av_rows,
                  title="Average distance", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Distance (nm)", legends=names,
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oall"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oall"), all_rows,
                  title="Distance", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Distance (nm)", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oxyz"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oxyz"), xyz_rows,
                  title="Distance", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="Distance (nm)", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oh"):
        _write_distance_histogram(ctx, state, samples, names)
    if state.is_set("oallstat"):
        legends = []
        for nm in names:
            legends.append(f"{nm} avg")
            legends.append(f"{nm} std.dev.")
        rows = []
        for pi in range(max_pairs):
            row = [float(pi)]
            for si in range(len(selections)):
                vals = pair_samples[si].get(pi, [])
                if vals:
                    mean = sum(vals) / len(vals)
                    var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals)
                    row.extend([mean, math.sqrt(var)])
                else:
                    row.extend([0.0, 0.0])
            rows.append(row)
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oallstat"), rows,
                  title="Statistics for individual distances",
                  xlabel="Distance index",
                  ylabel="Average/standard deviation (nm)",
                  legends=legends, xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  row_formatter=fmt)

    for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
        vals = samples[si]
        n = len(vals)
        mean = sum(vals) / n if n else float("nan")
        var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in vals) / n if n else float("nan")
        out_write(f"{compiled.name}:\n")
        out_write(f"  Number of samples:  {n}\n")
        out_write(f"  Average distance:   {mean:.5f}  nm\n")
        out_write(f"  Standard deviation: {math.sqrt(var):.5f}  nm\n")
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


def _write_distance_histogram(ctx, state, samples, names):
    length = float(state.value("len"))
    tol = float(state.value("tol"))
    binw = float(state.value("binw"))
    lo = length * (1.0 - tol)
    hi = length * (1.0 + tol)
    nbins = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi - lo) / binw))) if binw > 0 else 1
    rows = []
    counts = [[0] * nbins for _ in samples]
    for si, vals in enumerate(samples):
        for v in vals:
            idx = int((v - lo) / binw) if binw > 0 else 0
            idx = max(0, min(nbins - 1, idx))
            counts[si][idx] += 1
    for b in range(nbins):
        center = lo + (b + 0.5) * binw
        row = [center]
        for si, vals in enumerate(samples):
            total = len(vals)
            row.append(counts[si][b] / (total * binw) if total and binw else 0.0)
        rows.append(row)
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("oh"), rows,
              title="Distance histogram", xlabel="Distance (nm)",
              ylabel="Probability", legends=names,
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
              row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                  f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))

def residue_instances(frame):
    """Return [((resnr, resname, chain), [atom indices]), ...]."""
    residues = []
    for i, a in enumerate(frame.atoms):
        key = (a.resnr, a.resname, a.chain)
        if residues and residues[-1][0] == key:
            residues[-1][1].append(i)
        else:
            residues.append((key, [i]))
    return residues

SYNOPSIS

gmx pairdist [-f [<.xtc/.trr/...>]] [-s [<.tpr/.gro/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]]
             [-o [<.xvg>]] [-b <time>] [-e <time>] [-dt <time>] [-tu <enum>]
             [-fgroup <selection>] [-xvg <enum>] [-[no]rmpbc] [-[no]pbc]
             [-sf <file>] [-selrpos <enum>] [-seltype <enum>]
             [-cutoff <real>] [-type <enum>] [-refgrouping <enum>]
             [-selgrouping <enum>] [-ref <selection>] [-sel <selection>]

DESCRIPTION

gmx pairdist calculates pairwise distances between one reference selection
(given with -ref) and one or more other selections (given with -sel).  It can
calculate either the minimum distance (the default), or the maximum distance
(with -type max).  Distances to each selection provided with -sel are computed
independently.

By default, the global minimum/maximum distance is computed. To compute more
distances (e.g., minimum distances to each residue in -ref), use -refgrouping
and/or -selgrouping to specify how the positions within each selection should
be grouped.

Computed distances are written to the file specified with -o. If there are N
groups in -ref and M groups in the first selection in -sel, then the output
contains N*M columns for the first selection. The columns contain distances
like this: r1-s1, r2-s1, ..., r1-s2, r2-s2, ..., where rn is the n'th group in
-ref and sn is the n'th group in the other selection. The distances for the
second selection comes as separate columns after the first selection, and so
on.  If some selections are dynamic, only the selected positions are used in
the computation but the same number of columns is always written out.  If
there are no positions contributing to some group pair, then the cutoff value
is written (see below).

-cutoff sets a cutoff for the computed distances. If the result would contain
a distance over the cutoff, the cutoff value is written to the output file
instead. By default, no cutoff is used, but if you are not interested in
values beyond a cutoff, or if you know that the minimum distance is smaller
than a cutoff, you should set this option to allow the tool to use grid-based
searching and be significantly faster.

If you want to compute distances between fixed pairs, gmx distance may be a
more suitable tool.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx pairdist
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _group_positions(runner, positions, grouping):
    if grouping == "all":
        return [positions]
    if grouping == "none":
        return [[p] for p in positions]
    groups = []
    seen = {}
    for p in positions:
        if grouping == "res":
            key = runner.engine.atom_resindex[p.atoms[0]] if p.atoms else -1
        else:  # mol: one molecule for text topologies
            key = 0
        if key not in seen:
            seen[key] = len(groups)
            groups.append([])
        groups[seen[key]].append(p)
    return groups


def tool_pairdist(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    ref = runner.get_selections("ref", required=True, multiple=False)
    sels = runner.get_selections("sel", required=True, multiple=True)
    runner.register_output(state.file_value("o"), "xvg")
    refc = ref[0] if ref else None
    cutoff = float(state.value("cutoff"))
    typ = state.value("type") or "min"
    pbc = bool(state.value("pbc"))
    rows = []
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        refpos = runner.engine.evaluate_positions_node(refc.node, frame)
        refgroups = _group_positions(runner, refpos, state.value("refgrouping"))
        row = [frame.time]
        for compiled in sels:
            selpos = runner.engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
            selgroups = _group_positions(runner, selpos, state.value("selgrouping"))
            for sg in selgroups:
                for rg in refgroups:
                    vals = []
                    for a in rg:
                        for b in sg:
                            d, _v = _dist(a.pos, b.pos, frame.box, pbc)
                            vals.append(d)
                    if not vals:
                        value = cutoff if cutoff > 0 else float("nan")
                    else:
                        value = min(vals) if typ == "min" else max(vals)
                        if cutoff > 0 and value > cutoff:
                            value = cutoff
                    row.append(value)
        rows.append(row)
    runner.finish()
    title = "Minimum distance" if typ == "min" else "Maximum distance"
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), rows, title=title,
              xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Distance (nm)",
              legends=[c.name for c in sels],
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
              row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                  f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx gyrate
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_gyrate(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections("sel", required=True, multiple=False)
    runner.register_output(state.file_value("o"), "xvg")
    compiled = selections[0]
    mode = state.value("mode") or "mass"
    rows = []
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        positions = runner.engine.evaluate_positions_node(compiled.node, frame)
        weights = []
        for p in positions:
            if mode == "mass":
                weights.append(sum(runner.masses[a] for a in p.atoms))
            elif mode == "charge":
                weights.append(0.0)
            else:
                weights.append(float(len(p.atoms)) if p.atoms else 1.0)
        total = sum(weights)
        if total <= 0 or not positions:
            rows.append([frame.time, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
            continue
        center = [sum(weights[i] * positions[i].pos[d]
                      for i in range(len(positions))) / total
                  for d in range(3)]
        rg2 = sum(weights[i] * sum((positions[i].pos[d] - center[d]) ** 2
                                   for d in range(3))
                  for i in range(len(positions))) / total
        axis = []
        for ax in range(3):
            val = sum(weights[i] * sum(
                (positions[i].pos[d] - center[d]) ** 2
                for d in range(3) if d != ax)
                for i in range(len(positions))) / total
            axis.append(math.sqrt(val))
        rows.append([frame.time, math.sqrt(rg2)] + axis)
    runner.finish()
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), rows,
              title="Radius of gyration (total and around axes)",
              xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Radius (nm)",
              legends=["Rg", "Rg/sX/N", "Rg/sY/N", "Rg/sZ/N"],
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
              row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                  f" {v:f}" for v in r[1:]))
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx trajectory
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_trajectory(ctx, state):
    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections("select", required=True, multiple=True)
    for opt in ("ox", "ov", "of"):
        if state.is_set(opt):
            runner.register_output(state.file_value(opt), "xvg")
    # Component selection: if any of -x/-y/-z/-len is explicitly set,
    # only the explicitly enabled components are written.
    any_set = any(state.is_set(o) for o in ("x", "y", "z", "len"))
    comps = []
    if not any_set:
        comps = ["x", "y", "z"]
    else:
        if state.value("len"):
            comps.append("len")
        for c in ("x", "y", "z"):
            if state.is_set(c) and state.value(c):
                comps.append(c)
    possible = [_possible_positions(runner, c) for c in selections]
    ox_rows = []
    ov_rows = []
    of_rows = []
    have_vel = False
    for frame, raw in runner.iter_frames():
        def values_for(getter):
            vals = []
            for si, compiled in enumerate(selections):
                positions = runner.engine.evaluate_positions_node(
                    compiled.node, frame)
                by_key = {_position_key(runner.engine, p): p for p in positions}
                for pp in possible[si]:
                    p = by_key.get(_position_key(runner.engine, pp), pp)
                    vec = getter(frame, p)
                    for c in comps:
                        if c == "len":
                            vals.append(math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in vec)))
                        else:
                            vals.append(vec["xyz".index(c)])
            return vals

        if state.is_set("ox"):
            ox_rows.append([frame.time] + values_for(lambda f, p: p.pos))
        frame_has_vel = any(a.vel is not None for a in raw.atoms)
        if frame_has_vel:
            have_vel = True
        if state.is_set("ov") and frame_has_vel:
            def vel_of(f, p):
                if not p.atoms:
                    return (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
                vs = [f.atoms[a].vel or (0.0, 0.0, 0.0) for a in p.atoms
                      if a < len(f.atoms)]
                if not vs:
                    return (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
                return tuple(sum(v[d] for v in vs) / len(vs) for d in range(3))

            ov_rows.append([frame.time] + values_for(vel_of))
        if state.is_set("of"):
            # Text trajectories carry no forces.
            pass
    runner.finish()
    fmt = lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:])
    if state.is_set("ox"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("ox"), ox_rows, title="Coordinates",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Value [nm]", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("ov"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("ov"), ov_rows, title="Velocities",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Value [nm/ps]", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("of"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("of"), of_rows, title="Forces",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Value [kJ/mol nm]", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    return ctx.finish_success(0)

{"command":"cat >> app/gmxclone/ta_tools.py <<'PYEOF'


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx convert-trj
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _selection_is_atoms(node):
    kind = node[0]
    if kind == "atompos":
        return True
    if kind == "grouppos":
        from .selections import split_postype

        parsed = split_postype(node[1])
        return parsed is not None and parsed[1] == "atom"
    if kind in ("plus", "merge"):
        return _selection_is_atoms(node[1]) and _selection_is_atoms(node[2])
    if kind == "permute":
        return _selection_is_atoms(node[1])
    if kind == "var":
        return True
    return kind in ("all", "none", "group_index", "group_name", "not",
                    "and", "or", "string_prop", "num_list", "compare",
                    "same", "within", "insolidangle")


def tool_convert_trj(ctx, state):
    from .structures import file_extension as _ext_of
    from .selections import SelectionEvalError

    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    compiled = None
    if state.is_set("select"):
        sels = runner.get_selections("select", required=True, multiple=False)
        compiled = sels[0] if sels else None
        if compiled is not None and not _selection_is_atoms(compiled.node):
            raise GmxError(
                wrap_line(f"Selection '{compiled.name.strip()}' does not "
                          "evaluate to individual atoms. This is not allowed "
                          "in this context.") + "\n",
                title="Error in user input:",
                source="src/gromacs/selection/selectioncollection.cpp",
                line=856,
