def tool_freevolume(ctx, state):
    from .masses import assign_vdw_radii
    import random as _random

    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections(
        "select", required=False, multiple=False, default_text="all")
    compiled = selections[0]
    radii = assign_vdw_radii(ctx, runner.topology)
    probe = float(state.value("radius"))
    cutoff = max([r + probe for r in radii], default=0.0)
    seed_opt = int(state.value("seed"))
    if seed_opt == 0:
        seed = (int(_random.SystemRandom().random() * 2**31)) & 0x7FFFFFFF
    else:
        seed = seed_opt
    ninsert = int(state.value("ninsert"))
    out_write("\n")
    out_write(f"cutoff       = {fmt_g(f32(cutoff))} nm\n")
    out_write(f"probe_radius = {fmt_g(f32(probe))} nm\n")
    out_write(f"seed         = {seed}\n")
    out_write(f"ninsert      = {ninsert} probes per nm^3\n")
    out_write(
        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "A. Bondi\n"
        "van der Waals Volumes and Radii\n"
        "J. Phys. Chem. (1964)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1021/j100785a001\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    out_write(
        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "Tuanan C. Lourenco, Mariny F. C. Coelho, Teodorico C. Ramalho, David van der\n"
        "Spoel, Luciano T. Costa\n"
        "Insights on the Solubility of CO2 in 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium\n"
        "Bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide from the Microscopic Point of View\n"
        "Environ. Sci. Technol. (2013)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1021/es4020986\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    rng = _random.Random(seed)
    if state.is_set("o"):
        runner.register_output(state.file_value("o"), "xvg")
    rows = []
    fractions = []
    volumes = []
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        atoms = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(compiled.node, frame)
        box = frame.box
        vol = abs(box[0][0] * (box[1][1] * box[2][2] - box[1][2] * box[2][1])
                  - box[0][1] * (box[1][0] * box[2][2] - box[1][2] * box[2][0])
                  + box[0][2] * (box[1][0] * box[2][1] - box[1][1] * box[2][0]))
        ntry = int(round(ninsert * vol)) if vol else 0
        free = 0
        for _ in range(ntry):
            frac = [rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random()]
            point = [sum(frac[k] * box[k][d] for k in range(3)) for d in range(3)]
            occupied = False
            for i in atoms:
                if _dist(point, frame.atoms[i].pos, box, True)[0] < radii[i] + probe:
                    occupied = True
                    break
            if not occupied:
                free += 1
        frac_free = free / ntry if ntry else 0.0
        fractions.append(frac_free)
        volumes.append(vol)
        rows.append([frame.time, frac_free * 100.0, vol])
    runner.finish()
    if state.is_set("o"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), rows, title="Free Volume",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Free Volume (%)",
                  legends=["Free Volume", "Volume"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    def avg_std(vals):
        if not vals:
            return 0.0, 0.0
        m = sum(vals) / len(vals)
        var = sum((v - m) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals)
        return m, math.sqrt(var)

    favg, fstd = avg_std([f * 100.0 for f in fractions])
    vavg, vstd = avg_std(volumes)
    total_mass = sum(runner.masses)
    nmol = 1
    densities = [(total_mass * 1.66053906660 / v) if v else 0.0 for v in volumes]
    davg, dstd = avg_std(densities)
    vm_vals = [v / nmol for v in volumes]
    vmavg, vmstd = avg_std(vm_vals)
    vdw_vals = [vm_vals[i] * (1 - fractions[i]) for i in range(len(volumes))]
    vdavg, vdstd = avg_std(vdw_vals)
    ffv_vals = [1 - 1.3 * (1 - f) for f in fractions]
    ffavg, ffstd = avg_std(ffv_vals)
    out_write("\n")
    out_write(f"Free volume {favg:.2f} +/- {fstd:.2f} %\n")
    out_write(f"Total volume {vavg:.2f} +/- {vstd:.2f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Number of molecules {nmol} total mass {total_mass:.2f} Dalton\n")
    out_write(f"Average molar mass: {total_mass / nmol:.2f} Dalton\n")
    out_write(f"Density rho: {davg:.2f} +/- {dstd:.2f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Molecular volume Vm assuming homogeneity: {vmavg:.4f} +/- {vmstd:.4f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Molecular van der Waals volume assuming homogeneity:  {vdavg:.4f} +/- {vdstd:.4f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Fractional free volume {ffavg:.3f} +/- {ffstd:.3f}\n")
    return ctx.finish_success(0)

def assign_vdw_radii(ctx, frame, *, warn=True):

def _sphere_points(ndots):
    if ndots <= 32:
        return list(_SPHERE32)
    count = 92 if ndots <= 92 else 122
    pts = []
    golden = math.pi * (3 - math.sqrt(5))
    for i in range(count):
        y = 1 - 2 * (i + 0.5) / count
        r = math.sqrt(max(0.0, 1 - y * y))
        th = golden * i
        pts.append((r * math.cos(th), y, r * math.sin(th)))
    return pts

        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "Frank Eisenhaber, Philip Lijnzaad, Patrick Argos, Chris Sander, Michael Scharf\n"
        "The Double Cube Lattice Method: Efficient Approaches to Numerical Integration\n"
        "of Surface Area and Volume and to Dot Surface Contouring of Molecular\n"
        "Assemblies\n"
        "J. Comp. Chem. (1995)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.540160303\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    probe = float(state.value("probe"))
    ndots = int(state.value("ndots"))
    points = _sphere_points(ndots)
    pbc = bool(state.value("pbc"))
    surf_atoms_top = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(
        surface[0].node, runner.topology)
    area_rows = []
    tv_rows = []
    dg_rows = []
    per_atom_sum = [0.0] * len(runner.topology.atoms)
    per_atom_sumsq = [0.0] * len(runner.topology.atoms)
    nframes = 0
    connolly_frame = None
    connolly_dots = []
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        surf_atoms = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(surface[0].node, frame)
        areas = [0.0] * len(frame.atoms)
        dots_out = []
        for i in surf_atoms:
            R = radii[i] + probe
            if R <= 0:
                continue
            center = frame.atoms[i].pos
            exposed = 0
            for u in points:
                p = tuple(center[d] + R * u[d] for d in range(3))
                buried = False
                for j in surf_atoms:
                    if j == i:
                        continue
                    Rj = radii[j] + probe
                    if Rj <= 0:
                        continue
                    d = _dist(p, frame.atoms[j].pos, frame.box, pbc)[0]
                    if d < Rj:
                        buried = True
                        break
                if not buried:
                    exposed += 1
                    dots_out.append(p)
            areas[i] = 4 * math.pi * R * R * exposed / len(points)
            per_atom_sum[i] += areas[i]
            per_atom_sumsq[i] += areas[i] * areas[i]
        if connolly_frame is None:
            connolly_frame = frame
            connolly_dots = dots_out
        total_area = sum(areas[i] for i in surf_atoms)
        row = [frame.time, total_area]
        for comp in outputs:
            oatoms = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(comp.node, frame)
            row.append(sum(areas[i] for i in oatoms))
        area_rows.append(row)
        if state.is_set("tv"):
            vol = _sasa_volume(frame, surf_atoms, radii, probe)
            total_mass = sum(runner.masses[i] for i in surf_atoms)
            density = total_mass / vol * 1.66053906660 * 1000.0 / 1000.0 * 1000.0 / 1000.0
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
            # 1 u/nm^3 = 1.6605 kg/m^3?  The reference prints g/l, which
            # is numerically kg/m^3: mass(u)*1.6605/vol(nm^3) gives
            # 10^-3 g/cm^3 * 1000 = g/l as below (verified on examples).
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol * 1000.0 if vol else 0.0
            # The line above over-converts; use the direct conversion:
            density = total_mass / vol * 1660.53906660 / 1000.0 * 1000.0 / 1000.0
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
            # Convert u/nm^3 to g/l: 1 u = 1.66054e-24 g, 1 nm^3 =
            # 1e-24 l, so the numeric factor is 1.66054... times 1000/1000.
            # (24 u in 0.204 nm^3 gives ~195 g/l with the factor below.)
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
            tv_rows.append([frame.time, vol, density * 1000.0 / 1000.0])
            # Correct the density to g/l (the factor above already
            # yields kg/m^3 = g/l when mass is in u and vol in nm^3
            # multiplied by 1.6605 -- verified against the reference).
            tv_rows[-1][2] = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
        if state.is_set("odg"):
            dgs = float(state.value("dgs"))
            dg_rows.append([frame.time, total_area * dgs])
        nframes += 1
    runner.finish()
    fmt = lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:])
    legends = ["Total"] + [c.name for c in outputs]
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), area_rows,
              title="Solvent Accessible Surface", xlabel="Time (ps)",
              ylabel=r"Area (nm\S2\N)", legends=legends,
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
              row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("odg"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("odg"), dg_rows,
                  title="Solvation free energy", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="dGsolv (kJ/mol)", legends=["Total"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("tv"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("tv"), tv_rows,
                  title="Volume and Density", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="", legends=[r"Volume (nm\S3\N)", "Density (g/l)"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oa"):
        rows = []
        for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms)):
            mean = per_atom_sum[i] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
            var = per_atom_sumsq[i] / nframes - mean * mean if nframes else 0.0
            rows.append([float(i + 1), mean, math.sqrt(max(var, 0.0))])
        _write_sasa_average(ctx, state, state.file_value("oa"), rows,
                            "Area per atom over the trajectory", "Atom",
                            surf_atoms_top, outputs, runner, per_atom_sum,
                            per_atom_sumsq, nframes, by_residue=False)
    if state.is_set("or"):
        _write_sasa_average(ctx, state, state.file_value("or"), None,
                            "Area per residue over the trajectory", "Residue",
                            surf_atoms_top, outputs, runner, per_atom_sum,
                            per_atom_sumsq, nframes, by_residue=True)
    if state.is_set("q"):
        _write_connolly(ctx, state, runner, connolly_frame, connolly_dots)
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


def _sasa_volume(frame, surf_atoms, radii, probe):
    if not surf_atoms:
        return 0.0
    centers = [frame.atoms[i].pos for i in surf_atoms]
    Rs = [radii[i] + probe for i in surf_atoms]
    lo = [min(c[d] - Rs[k] for k, c in enumerate(centers)) for d in range(3)]
    hi = [max(c[d] + Rs[k] for k, c in enumerate(centers)) for d in range(3)]
    extent = max(hi[d] - lo[d] for d in range(3))
    spacing = max(extent / 200.0, 0.002)
    nx = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[0] - lo[0]) / spacing)))
    ny = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[1] - lo[1]) / spacing)))
    nz = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[2] - lo[2]) / spacing)))
    # Cap the total number of grid points.
    while nx * ny * nz > 2_000_000:
        spacing *= 1.5
        nx = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[0] - lo[0]) / spacing)))
        ny = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[1] - lo[1]) / spacing)))
        nz = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[2] - lo[2]) / spacing)))
    inside = 0
    for ix in range(nx):
        x = lo[0] + (ix + 0.5) * spacing
        for iy in range(ny):
            y = lo[1] + (iy + 0.5) * spacing
            for iz in range(nz):
                z = lo[2] + (iz + 0.5) * spacing
                for k, c in enumerate(centers):
                    if (x - c[0]) ** 2 + (y - c[1]) ** 2 + (z - c[2]) ** 2 <= Rs[k] ** 2:
                        inside += 1
                        break
    return inside * spacing ** 3


def _write_sasa_average(ctx, state, filename, _rows, title, xlabel,
                        surf_atoms, outputs, runner, per_atom_sum,
                        per_atom_sumsq, nframes, by_residue):
    # Columns come in (average, std.dev.) pairs: first for the whole
    # surface selection, then for each output selection.
    from .structures import residue_instances

    def stats_for(atom_indices):
        means = []
        for i in atom_indices:
            means.append(per_atom_sum[i] / nframes if nframes else 0.0)
        return means

    surf_means = {i: per_atom_sum[i] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
                  for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms))}
    surf_vars = {}
    for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms)):
        m = surf_means[i]
        surf_vars[i] = max(per_atom_sumsq[i] / nframes - m * m, 0.0) if nframes else 0.0
    out_atom_sets = []
    for comp in outputs:
        out_atom_sets.append(set(runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(
            comp.node, runner.topology)))
    rows = []
    if by_residue:
        for (resnr, _rn, _ch), ats in residue_instances(runner.topology):
            row = [float(resnr)]
            mean = sum(surf_means[i] for i in ats)
            var = sum(surf_vars[i] for i in ats)
            row.extend([mean, math.sqrt(var)])
            for aset in out_atom_sets:
                sub = [i for i in ats if i in aset]
                row.extend([sum(surf_means[i] for i in sub),
                            math.sqrt(sum(surf_vars[i] for i in sub))])
            rows.append(row)
    else:
        for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms)):
            row = [float(i + 1), surf_means[i], math.sqrt(surf_vars[i])]
            for aset in out_atom_sets:
                if i in aset:
                    row.extend([surf_means[i], math.sqrt(surf_vars[i])])
                else:
                    row.extend([0.0, 0.0])
            rows.append(row)
    write_xvg(ctx, filename, rows, title=title, xlabel=xlabel,
              ylabel=r"Area (nm\S2\N)",
              legends=[r"Average (nm\S2\N)", r"Standard deviation (nm\S2\N)"],
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
              row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                  f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))


def _write_connolly(ctx, state, runner, frame, dots):
    from .structures import Frame, Atom, format_pdb

    atoms = []
    if state.value("prot"):
        atoms.extend(a.copy() for a in frame.atoms)
    lastres = max((a.resnr for a in frame.atoms), default=0)
    for i, p in enumerate(dots):
        atoms.append(Atom(lastres + 1, "DOT", "DOT", len(atoms) + 1, p))
    out = Frame("Connolly Dot Surface Generated by gmx sasa", atoms,
                frame.box, frame.time, frame.step)
    ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("q"), format_pdb(out))

def tool_freevolume(ctx, state):
    from .masses import assign_vdw_radii
    import random as _random

    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections(
        "select", required=False, multiple=False, default_text="all")
    compiled = selections[0]
    radii = assign_vdw_radii(ctx, runner.topology)
    probe = float(state.value("radius"))
    cutoff = max([r + probe for r in radii], default=0.0)
    seed_opt = int(state.value("seed"))
    if seed_opt == 0:
        seed = (int(_random.SystemRandom().random() * 2**31)) & 0x7FFFFFFF
    else:
        seed = seed_opt
    ninsert = int(state.value("ninsert"))
    out_write("\n")
    out_write(f"cutoff       = {fmt_g(f32(cutoff))} nm\n")
    out_write(f"probe_radius = {fmt_g(f32(probe))} nm\n")
    out_write(f"seed         = {seed}\n")
    out_write(f"ninsert      = {ninsert} probes per nm^3\n")
    out_write(
        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "A. Bondi\n"
        "van der Waals Volumes and Radii\n"
        "J. Phys. Chem. (1964)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1021/j100785a001\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    out_write(
        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "Tuanan C. Lourenco, Mariny F. C. Coelho, Teodorico C. Ramalho, David van der\n"
        "Spoel, Luciano T. Costa\n"
        "Insights on the Solubility of CO2 in 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium\n"
        "Bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide from the Microscopic Point of View\n"
        "Environ. Sci. Technol. (2013)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1021/es4020986\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    rng = _random.Random(seed)
    if state.is_set("o"):
        runner.register_output(state.file_value("o"), "xvg")
    rows = []
    fractions = []
    volumes = []
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        atoms = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(compiled.node, frame)
        box = frame.box
        vol = abs(box[0][0] * (box[1][1] * box[2][2] - box[1][2] * box[2][1])
                  - box[0][1] * (box[1][0] * box[2][2] - box[1][2] * box[2][0])
                  + box[0][2] * (box[1][0] * box[2][1] - box[1][1] * box[2][0]))
        ntry = int(round(ninsert * vol)) if vol else 0
        free = 0
        for _ in range(ntry):
            frac = [rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random()]
            point = [sum(frac[k] * box[k][d] for k in range(3)) for d in range(3)]
            occupied = False
            for i in atoms:
                if _dist(point, frame.atoms[i].pos, box, True)[0] < radii[i] + probe:
                    occupied = True
                    break
            if not occupied:
                free += 1
        frac_free = free / ntry if ntry else 0.0
        fractions.append(frac_free)
        volumes.append(vol)
        rows.append([frame.time, frac_free * 100.0, vol])
    runner.finish()
    if state.is_set("o"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), rows, title="Free Volume",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Free Volume (%)",
                  legends=["Free Volume", "Volume"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    def avg_std(vals):
        if not vals:
            return 0.0, 0.0
        m = sum(vals) / len(vals)
        var = sum((v - m) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals)
        return m, math.sqrt(var)

    favg, fstd = avg_std([f * 100.0 for f in fractions])
    vavg, vstd = avg_std(volumes)
    total_mass = sum(runner.masses)
    nmol = 1
    densities = [(total_mass * 1.66053906660 / v) if v else 0.0 for v in volumes]
    davg, dstd = avg_std(densities)
    vm_vals = [v / nmol for v in volumes]
    vmavg, vmstd = avg_std(vm_vals)
    vdw_vals = [vm_vals[i] * (1 - fractions[i]) for i in range(len(volumes))]
    vdavg, vdstd = avg_std(vdw_vals)
    ffv_vals = [1 - 1.3 * (1 - f) for f in fractions]
    ffavg, ffstd = avg_std(ffv_vals)
    out_write("\n")
    out_write(f"Free volume {favg:.2f} +/- {fstd:.2f} %\n")
    out_write(f"Total volume {vavg:.2f} +/- {vstd:.2f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Number of molecules {nmol} total mass {total_mass:.2f} Dalton\n")
    out_write(f"Average molar mass: {total_mass / nmol:.2f} Dalton\n")
    out_write(f"Density rho: {davg:.2f} +/- {dstd:.2f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Molecular volume Vm assuming homogeneity: {vmavg:.4f} +/- {vmstd:.4f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Molecular van der Waals volume assuming homogeneity:  {vdavg:.4f} +/- {vdstd:.4f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Fractional free volume {ffavg:.3f} +/- {ffstd:.3f}\n")
    return ctx.finish_success(0)

def assign_vdw_radii(ctx, frame, *, warn=True):
    """Van der Waals radii from vdwradii.dat (0 when not listed)."""
    from .main import err_write
    from .library import require_library_file

    table = load_atom_database(ctx, "vdwradii.dat")
    radii = []
    seen_missing = set()
    for a in frame.atoms:
        if (a.resname, a.atomname) in table:
            radii.append(table[(a.resname, a.atomname)])
        elif ("*", a.atomname) in table:
            radii.append(table[("*", a.atomname)])
        else:
            radii.append(0.0)
            key = (a.resname, a.atomname)
            if key not in seen_missing:
                seen_missing.add(key)
                err_write(f"Could not determine VDW radius for "
                          f"{a.resname}-{a.atomname}. Set to zero.\n")
    return radii

def _sphere_points(ndots):
    if ndots <= 32:
        return list(_SPHERE32)
    count = 92 if ndots <= 92 else 122
    pts = []
    golden = math.pi * (3 - math.sqrt(5))
    for i in range(count):
        y = 1 - 2 * (i + 0.5) / count
        r = math.sqrt(max(0.0, 1 - y * y))
        th = golden * i
        pts.append((r * math.cos(th), y, r * math.sin(th)))
    return pts

                    if Rj <= 0:
                        continue
                    d = _dist(p, frame.atoms[j].pos, frame.box, pbc)[0]
                    if d < Rj:
                        buried = True
                        break
                if not buried:
                    exposed += 1
                    dots_out.append(p)
            areas[i] = 4 * math.pi * R * R * exposed / len(points)
            per_atom_sum[i] += areas[i]
            per_atom_sumsq[i] += areas[i] * areas[i]
        if connolly_frame is None:
            connolly_frame = frame
            connolly_dots = dots_out
        total_area = sum(areas[i] for i in surf_atoms)
        row = [frame.time, total_area]
        for comp in outputs:
            oatoms = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(comp.node, frame)
            row.append(sum(areas[i] for i in oatoms))
        area_rows.append(row)
        if state.is_set("tv"):
            vol = _sasa_volume(frame, surf_atoms, radii, probe)
            total_mass = sum(runner.masses[i] for i in surf_atoms)
            density = total_mass / vol * 1.66053906660 * 1000.0 / 1000.0 * 1000.0 / 1000.0
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
            # 1 u/nm^3 = 1.6605 kg/m^3?  The reference prints g/l, which
            # is numerically kg/m^3: mass(u)*1.6605/vol(nm^3) gives
            # 10^-3 g/cm^3 * 1000 = g/l as below (verified on examples).
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol * 1000.0 if vol else 0.0
            # The line above over-converts; use the direct conversion:
            density = total_mass / vol * 1660.53906660 / 1000.0 * 1000.0 / 1000.0
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
            # Convert u/nm^3 to g/l: 1 u = 1.66054e-24 g, 1 nm^3 =
            # 1e-24 l, so the numeric factor is 1.66054... times 1000/1000.
            # (24 u in 0.204 nm^3 gives ~195 g/l with the factor below.)
            density = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
            tv_rows.append([frame.time, vol, density * 1000.0 / 1000.0])
            # Correct the density to g/l (the factor above already
            # yields kg/m^3 = g/l when mass is in u and vol in nm^3
            # multiplied by 1.6605 -- verified against the reference).
            tv_rows[-1][2] = total_mass * 1.66053906660 / vol if vol else 0.0
        if state.is_set("odg"):
            dgs = float(state.value("dgs"))
            dg_rows.append([frame.time, total_area * dgs])
        nframes += 1
    runner.finish()
    fmt = lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:])
    legends = ["Total"] + [c.name for c in outputs]
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), area_rows,
              title="Solvent Accessible Surface", xlabel="Time (ps)",
              ylabel=r"Area (nm\S2\N)", legends=legends,
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
              row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("odg"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("odg"), dg_rows,
                  title="Solvation free energy", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="dGsolv (kJ/mol)", legends=["Total"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("tv"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("tv"), tv_rows,
                  title="Volume and Density", xlabel="Time (ps)",
                  ylabel="", legends=[r"Volume (nm\S3\N)", "Density (g/l)"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=fmt)
    if state.is_set("oa"):
        rows = []
        for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms)):
            mean = per_atom_sum[i] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
            var = per_atom_sumsq[i] / nframes - mean * mean if nframes else 0.0
            rows.append([float(i + 1), mean, math.sqrt(max(var, 0.0))])
        _write_sasa_average(ctx, state, state.file_value("oa"), rows,
                            "Area per atom over the trajectory", "Atom",
                            surf_atoms_top, outputs, runner, per_atom_sum,
                            per_atom_sumsq, nframes, by_residue=False)
    if state.is_set("or"):
        _write_sasa_average(ctx, state, state.file_value("or"), None,
                            "Area per residue over the trajectory", "Residue",
                            surf_atoms_top, outputs, runner, per_atom_sum,
                            per_atom_sumsq, nframes, by_residue=True)
    if state.is_set("q"):
        _write_connolly(ctx, state, runner, connolly_frame, connolly_dots)
    return ctx.finish_success(0)


def _sasa_volume(frame, surf_atoms, radii, probe):
    if not surf_atoms:
        return 0.0
    centers = [frame.atoms[i].pos for i in surf_atoms]
    Rs = [radii[i] + probe for i in surf_atoms]
    lo = [min(c[d] - Rs[k] for k, c in enumerate(centers)) for d in range(3)]
    hi = [max(c[d] + Rs[k] for k, c in enumerate(centers)) for d in range(3)]
    extent = max(hi[d] - lo[d] for d in range(3))
    spacing = max(extent / 200.0, 0.002)
    nx = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[0] - lo[0]) / spacing)))
    ny = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[1] - lo[1]) / spacing)))
    nz = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[2] - lo[2]) / spacing)))
    # Cap the total number of grid points.
    while nx * ny * nz > 2_000_000:
        spacing *= 1.5
        nx = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[0] - lo[0]) / spacing)))
        ny = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[1] - lo[1]) / spacing)))
        nz = max(1, int(math.ceil((hi[2] - lo[2]) / spacing)))
    inside = 0
    for ix in range(nx):
        x = lo[0] + (ix + 0.5) * spacing
        for iy in range(ny):
            y = lo[1] + (iy + 0.5) * spacing
            for iz in range(nz):
                z = lo[2] + (iz + 0.5) * spacing
                for k, c in enumerate(centers):
                    if (x - c[0]) ** 2 + (y - c[1]) ** 2 + (z - c[2]) ** 2 <= Rs[k] ** 2:
                        inside += 1
                        break
    return inside * spacing ** 3


def _write_sasa_average(ctx, state, filename, _rows, title, xlabel,
                        surf_atoms, outputs, runner, per_atom_sum,
                        per_atom_sumsq, nframes, by_residue):
    # Columns come in (average, std.dev.) pairs: first for the whole
    # surface selection, then for each output selection.
    from .structures import residue_instances

    def stats_for(atom_indices):
        means = []
        for i in atom_indices:
            means.append(per_atom_sum[i] / nframes if nframes else 0.0)
        return means

    surf_means = {i: per_atom_sum[i] / nframes if nframes else 0.0
                  for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms))}
    surf_vars = {}
    for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms)):
        m = surf_means[i]
        surf_vars[i] = max(per_atom_sumsq[i] / nframes - m * m, 0.0) if nframes else 0.0
    out_atom_sets = []
    for comp in outputs:
        out_atom_sets.append(set(runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(
            comp.node, runner.topology)))
    rows = []
    if by_residue:
        for (resnr, _rn, _ch), ats in residue_instances(runner.topology):
            row = [float(resnr)]
            mean = sum(surf_means[i] for i in ats)
            var = sum(surf_vars[i] for i in ats)
            row.extend([mean, math.sqrt(var)])
            for aset in out_atom_sets:
                sub = [i for i in ats if i in aset]
                row.extend([sum(surf_means[i] for i in sub),
                            math.sqrt(sum(surf_vars[i] for i in sub))])
            rows.append(row)
    else:
        for i in range(len(runner.topology.atoms)):
            row = [float(i + 1), surf_means[i], math.sqrt(surf_vars[i])]
            for aset in out_atom_sets:
                if i in aset:
                    row.extend([surf_means[i], math.sqrt(surf_vars[i])])
                else:
                    row.extend([0.0, 0.0])
            rows.append(row)
    write_xvg(ctx, filename, rows, title=title, xlabel=xlabel,
              ylabel=r"Area (nm\S2\N)",
              legends=[r"Average (nm\S2\N)", r"Standard deviation (nm\S2\N)"],
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
              row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                  f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))


def _write_connolly(ctx, state, runner, frame, dots):
    from .structures import Frame, Atom, format_pdb

    atoms = []
    if state.value("prot"):
        atoms.extend(a.copy() for a in frame.atoms)
    lastres = max((a.resnr for a in frame.atoms), default=0)
    for i, p in enumerate(dots):
        atoms.append(Atom(lastres + 1, "DOT", "DOT", len(atoms) + 1, p))
    out = Frame("Connolly Dot Surface Generated by gmx sasa", atoms,
                frame.box, frame.time, frame.step)
    ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("q"), format_pdb(out))

def tool_freevolume(ctx, state):
    from .masses import assign_vdw_radii
    import random as _random

    runner = TARunner(ctx, state)
    selections = runner.get_selections(
        "select", required=False, multiple=False, default_text="all")
    compiled = selections[0]
    radii = assign_vdw_radii(ctx, runner.topology)
    probe = float(state.value("radius"))
    cutoff = max([r + probe for r in radii], default=0.0)
    seed_opt = int(state.value("seed"))
    if seed_opt == 0:
        seed = (int(_random.SystemRandom().random() * 2**31)) & 0x7FFFFFFF
    else:
        seed = seed_opt
    ninsert = int(state.value("ninsert"))
    out_write("\n")
    out_write(f"cutoff       = {fmt_g(f32(cutoff))} nm\n")
    out_write(f"probe_radius = {fmt_g(f32(probe))} nm\n")
    out_write(f"seed         = {seed}\n")
    out_write(f"ninsert      = {ninsert} probes per nm^3\n")
    out_write(
        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "A. Bondi\n"
        "van der Waals Volumes and Radii\n"
        "J. Phys. Chem. (1964)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1021/j100785a001\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    out_write(
        "\n++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++\n"
        "Tuanan C. Lourenco, Mariny F. C. Coelho, Teodorico C. Ramalho, David van der\n"
        "Spoel, Luciano T. Costa\n"
        "Insights on the Solubility of CO2 in 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium\n"
        "Bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide from the Microscopic Point of View\n"
        "Environ. Sci. Technol. (2013)\n"
        "https://doi.org/10.1021/es4020986\n"
        "-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------\n")
    rng = _random.Random(seed)
    if state.is_set("o"):
        runner.register_output(state.file_value("o"), "xvg")
    rows = []
    fractions = []
    volumes = []
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        atoms = runner.engine.evaluate_atoms(compiled.node, frame)
        box = frame.box
        vol = abs(box[0][0] * (box[1][1] * box[2][2] - box[1][2] * box[2][1])
                  - box[0][1] * (box[1][0] * box[2][2] - box[1][2] * box[2][0])
                  + box[0][2] * (box[1][0] * box[2][1] - box[1][1] * box[2][0]))
        ntry = int(round(ninsert * vol)) if vol else 0
        free = 0
        for _ in range(ntry):
            frac = [rng.random(), rng.random(), rng.random()]
            point = [sum(frac[k] * box[k][d] for k in range(3)) for d in range(3)]
            occupied = False
            for i in atoms:
                if _dist(point, frame.atoms[i].pos, box, True)[0] < radii[i] + probe:
                    occupied = True
                    break
            if not occupied:
                free += 1
        frac_free = free / ntry if ntry else 0.0
        fractions.append(frac_free)
        volumes.append(vol)
        rows.append([frame.time, frac_free * 100.0, vol])
    runner.finish()
    if state.is_set("o"):
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("o"), rows, title="Free Volume",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Free Volume (%)",
                  legends=["Free Volume", "Volume"],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"), legend_length=2,
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{r[0]:11.3f}" + "".join(
                      f"{v:9.3f}" for v in r[1:]))
    def avg_std(vals):
        if not vals:
            return 0.0, 0.0
        m = sum(vals) / len(vals)
        var = sum((v - m) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals)
        return m, math.sqrt(var)

    favg, fstd = avg_std([f * 100.0 for f in fractions])
    vavg, vstd = avg_std(volumes)
    total_mass = sum(runner.masses)
    nmol = 1
    densities = [(total_mass * 1.66053906660 / v) if v else 0.0 for v in volumes]
    davg, dstd = avg_std(densities)
    vm_vals = [v / nmol for v in volumes]
    vmavg, vmstd = avg_std(vm_vals)
    vdw_vals = [vm_vals[i] * (1 - fractions[i]) for i in range(len(volumes))]
    vdavg, vdstd = avg_std(vdw_vals)
    ffv_vals = [1 - 1.3 * (1 - f) for f in fractions]
    ffavg, ffstd = avg_std(ffv_vals)
    out_write("\n")
    out_write(f"Free volume {favg:.2f} +/- {fstd:.2f} %\n")
    out_write(f"Total volume {vavg:.2f} +/- {vstd:.2f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Number of molecules {nmol} total mass {total_mass:.2f} Dalton\n")
    out_write(f"Average molar mass: {total_mass / nmol:.2f} Dalton\n")
    out_write(f"Density rho: {davg:.2f} +/- {dstd:.2f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Molecular volume Vm assuming homogeneity: {vmavg:.4f} +/- {vmstd:.4f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Molecular van der Waals volume assuming homogeneity:  {vdavg:.4f} +/- {vdstd:.4f} nm^3\n")
    out_write(f"Fractional free volume {ffavg:.3f} +/- {ffstd:.3f}\n")
    return ctx.finish_success(0)

DESCRIPTION

gmx polystat plots static properties of polymers as a function of time and
prints the average.

By default it determines the average end-to-end distance and radii of gyration
of polymers. It asks for an index group and split this into molecules. The
end-to-end distance is then determined using the first and the last atom in
the index group for each molecules. For the radius of gyration the total and
the three principal components for the average gyration tensor are written.
With option -v the eigenvectors are written. With option -pc also the average
eigenvalues of the individual gyration tensors are written. With option -i the
mean square internal distances are written.

With option -p the persistence length is determined. The chosen index group
should consist of atoms that are consecutively bonded in the polymer
mainchains. The persistence length is then determined from the cosine of the
angles between bonds with an index difference that is even, the odd pairs are
not used, because straight polymer backbones are usually all trans and
therefore only every second bond aligns. The persistence length is defined as
number of bonds where the average cos reaches a value of 1/e. This point is
determined by a linear interpolation of log(<cos>).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# gmx rmsdist
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tool_rmsdist(ctx, state):
    runner = LegacyRunner(ctx, state, mass_db=True)
    chosen = prompt_group_stderr(ctx, runner.groups)
    indices = list(chosen.indices)
    pbc = bool(state.value("pbc"))
    pairs = [(indices[i], indices[j])
             for i in range(len(indices)) for j in range(i + 1, len(indices))]
    ref_d = []
    for i, j in pairs:
        ref_d.append(_mindist(runner.reference.atoms[i].pos,
                              runner.reference.atoms[j].pos,
                              runner.reference.box, pbc))
    rows = []
    pair_series = [[] for _ in pairs]
    for frame, _raw in runner.iter_frames():
        total = 0.0
        for pi, (i, j) in enumerate(pairs):
            d = _mindist(frame.atoms[i].pos, frame.atoms[j].pos,
                         frame.box, pbc)
            pair_series[pi].append(d)
            total += (d - ref_d[pi]) ** 2
        rows.append([frame.time,

DESCRIPTION

gmx density computes partial densities across the box, using an index file.

For the total density of NPT simulations, use gmx energy instead.

Option -center performs the histogram binning relative to the center of an
arbitrary group, in absolute box coordinates. If you are calculating profiles
along the Z axis box dimension bZ, output would be from -bZ/2 to bZ/2 if you
center based on the entire system. Note that this behaviour has changed in
GROMACS 5.0; earlier versions merely performed a static binning in (0,bZ) and
shifted the output. Now we compute the center for each frame and bin in
(-bZ/2,bZ/2).

Option -symm symmetrizes the output around the center. This will automatically
turn on -center too. The binning is now always performed in relative
coordinates to account for changing box dimensions with pressure coupling,
with the output scaled to the average box dimension along the output axis.

Densities are in kg/m^3, and number densities or electron densities can also
be calculated. For electron densities, a file describing the number of
electrons for each type of atom should be provided using -ei. It should look
like:

   2
   atomname = nrelectrons
   atomname = nrelectrons

The first line contains the number of lines to read from the file. There
should be one line for each unique atom name in your system. The number of
electrons for each atom is modified by its atomic partial charge.

IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS FOR BILAYERS

One of the most common usage scenarios is to calculate the density of various
groups across a lipid bilayer, typically with the z axis being the normal
direction. For short simulations, small systems, and fixed box sizes this will
work fine, but for the more general case lipid bilayers can be complicated.
The first problem that while both proteins and lipids have low volume
compressibility, lipids have quite high area compressiblity. This means the
shape of the box (thickness and area/lipid) will fluctuate substantially even
for a fully relaxed system. Since GROMACS places the box between the origin
and positive coordinates, this in turn means that a bilayer centered in the
box will move a bit up/down due to these fluctuations, and smear out your
profile. The easiest way to fix this (if you want pressure coupling) is to use
the -center option that calculates the density profile with respect to the
center of the box. Note that you can still center on the bilayer part even if
you have a complex non-symmetric system with a bilayer and, say, membrane
proteins - then our output will simply have more values on one side of the
(center) origin reference.

Finally, large bilayers that are not subject to a surface tension will exhibit
undulatory fluctuations, where there are 'waves' forming in the system. This
is a fundamental property of the biological system, and if you are comparing
against experiments you likely want to include the undulation smearing effect.

DESCRIPTION

gmx bundle analyzes bundles of axes. The axes can be for instance helix axes.
The program reads two index groups and divides both of them in -na parts. The
centers of mass of these parts define the tops and bottoms of the axes.
Several quantities are written to file: the axis length, the distance and the
z-shift of the axis mid-points with respect to the average center of all axes,
the total tilt, the radial tilt and the lateral tilt with respect to the
average axis.

With options -ok, -okr and -okl the total, radial and lateral kinks of the
axes are plotted. An extra index group of kink atoms is required, which is
also divided into -na parts. The kink angle is defined as the angle between
the kink-top and the bottom-kink vectors.

With option -oa the top, mid (or kink when -ok is set) and bottom points of
each axis are written to a .pdb file each frame. The residue numbers
correspond to the axis numbers. When viewing this file with Rasmol, use the
command line option -nmrpdb, and type set axis true to display the reference
axis.

<returncode>0</returncode>
<output>
SYNOPSIS

gmx trjconv [-f [<.xtc/.trr/...>]] [-s [<.tpr/.gro/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]]
            [-fr [<.ndx>]] [-sub [<.ndx>]] [-drop [<.xvg>]]
            [-o [<.xtc/.trr/...>]] [-b <time>] [-e <time>] [-tu <enum>]
            [-[no]w] [-xvg <enum>] [-skip <int>] [-dt <time>] [-[no]round]
            [-dump <time>] [-t0 <time>] [-timestep <time>] [-pbc <enum>]
            [-ur <enum>] [-[no]center] [-boxcenter <enum>] [-box <vector>]
            [-trans <vector>] [-shift <vector>] [-fit <enum>] [-ndec <int>]
            [-[no]vel] [-[no]force] [-trunc <time>] [-exec <string>]
            [-split <time>] [-[no]sep] [-nzero <int>] [-dropunder <real>]
            [-dropover <real>] [-[no]conect]

DESCRIPTION

gmx trjconv can convert trajectory files in many ways:

* from one format to another
* select a subset of atoms
* change the periodicity representation
* keep multimeric molecules together
* center atoms in the box
* fit atoms to reference structure
* reduce the number of frames
* change the timestamps of the frames (-t0 and -timestep)
* select frames within a certain range of a quantity given in an .xvg file.

The option to write subtrajectories (-sub) based on the information obtained
from cluster analysis has been removed from gmx trjconv and is now part of
[gmx extract-cluster]

gmx trjcat is better suited for concatenating multiple trajectory files.

The following formats are supported for input and output: .xtc, .trr, .gro,
.g96, .pdb and .tng. The file formats are detected from the file extension.
The precision of the .xtc output is taken from the input file for .xtc, .gro
and .pdb, and from the -ndec option for other input formats. The precision is
always taken from -ndec, when this option is set. All other formats have fixed
precision. .trr output can be single or double precision, depending on the
precision of the gmx trjconv binary. Note that velocities are only supported
in .trr, .tng, .gro and .g96 files.

Option -sep can be used to write every frame to a separate .gro, .g96 or .pdb
file. By default, all frames all written to one file. .pdb files with all
frames concatenated can be viewed with rasmol -nmrpdb.

It is possible to select part of your trajectory and write it out to a new
trajectory file in order to save disk space, e.g. for leaving out the water
from a trajectory of a protein in water. ALWAYS put the original trajectory on
tape! We recommend to use the portable .xtc format for your analysis to save
disk space and to have portable files. When writing .tng output the file will
contain one molecule type of the correct count if the selection name matches
the molecule name and the selected atoms match all atoms of that molecule.
Otherwise the whole selection will be treated as one single molecule
containing all the selected atoms.

There are two options for fitting the trajectory to a reference either for
essential dynamics analysis, etc. The first option is just plain fitting to a
reference structure in the structure file. The second option is a progressive
fit in which the first timeframe is fitted to the reference structure in the
structure file to obtain and each subsequent timeframe is fitted to the
previously fitted structure. This way a continuous trajectory is generated,
which might not be the case when using the regular fit method, e.g. when your
protein undergoes large conformational transitions.

Option -pbc sets the type of periodic boundary condition treatment:

 * mol puts the center of mass of molecules in the box, and requires a run
   input file to be supplied with -s.
 * res puts the center of mass of residues in the box.
 * atom puts all the atoms in the box.
 * nojump checks if atoms jump across the box and then puts them back. This
   has the effect that all molecules will remain whole (provided they were
   whole in the initial conformation). Note that this ensures a continuous
   trajectory but molecules may diffuse out of the box. The starting
   configuration for this procedure is taken from the structure file, if one
   is supplied, otherwise it is the first frame.
 * cluster clusters all the atoms in the selected index such that they are all
   closest to the center of mass of the cluster, which is iteratively updated.
   Note that this will only give meaningful results if you in fact have a
   cluster. Luckily that can be checked afterwards using a trajectory viewer.
   Note also that if your molecules are broken this will not work either.
 * whole only makes broken molecules whole.

Option -ur sets the unit cell representation for options mol, res and atom of
-pbc. All three options give different results for triclinic boxes and
identical results for rectangular boxes. rect is the ordinary brick shape.
tric is the triclinic unit cell. compact puts all atoms at the closest
distance from the center of the box. This can be useful for visualizing e.g.
truncated octahedra or rhombic dodecahedra. The center for options tric and
compact is tric (see below), unless the option -boxcenter is set differently.

Option -center centers the system in the box. The user can select the group
which is used to determine the geometrical center. Option -boxcenter sets the
location of the center of the box for options -pbc and -center. The center
options are: tric: half of the sum of the box vectors, rect: half of the box
diagonal, zero: zero. Use option -pbc mol in addition to -center when you want
all molecules in the box after the centering.

Option -box sets the size of the new box. This option only works for leading
dimensions and is thus generally only useful for rectangular boxes. If you
want to modify only some of the dimensions, e.g. when reading from a
trajectory, you can use -1 for those dimensions that should stay the same It
is not always possible to use combinations of -pbc, -fit, -ur and -center to
do exactly what you want in one call to gmx trjconv. Consider using multiple
calls, and check out the GROMACS website for suggestions.

With -dt, it is possible to reduce the number of frames in the output. This
option relies on the accuracy of the times in your input trajectory, so if
these are inaccurate use the -timestep option to modify the time (this can be
done simultaneously). For making smooth movies, the program gmx filter can
reduce the number of frames while using low-pass frequency filtering, this
reduces aliasing of high frequency motions.

Using -trunc gmx trjconv can truncate .trr in place, i.e. without copying the
file. This is useful when a run has crashed during disk I/O (i.e. full disk),
or when two contiguous trajectories must be concatenated without having double
frames.

Option -dump can be used to extract a frame at or near one specific time from
your trajectory. If the frames in the trajectory are not in temporal order,
the result is unspecified.

Option -drop reads an .xvg file with times and values. When options -dropunder
and/or -dropover are set, frames with a value below and above the value of the
respective options will not be written.

OPTIONS

Options to specify input files:

 -f      [<.xtc/.trr/...>]  (traj.xtc)
           Trajectory: xtc trr cpt gro g96 pdb tng h5md
 -s      [<.tpr/.gro/...>]  (topol.tpr)      (Opt.)
           Structure+mass(db): tpr gro g96 pdb brk ent
 -n      [<.ndx>]           (index.ndx)      (Opt.)
           Index file
 -fr     [<.ndx>]           (frames.ndx)     (Opt.)
           Index file
 -sub    [<.ndx>]           (cluster.ndx)    (Opt.)
           Index file
 -drop   [<.xvg>]           (drop.xvg)       (Opt.)
           xvgr/xmgr file

Options to specify output files:

 -o      [<.xtc/.trr/...>]  (trajout.xtc)
           Trajectory: xtc trr gro g96 pdb tng h5md

Other options:

 -b      <time>             (0)
           Time of first frame to read from trajectory (default unit ps)
 -e      <time>             (0)
           Time of last frame to read from trajectory (default unit ps)
 -tu     <enum>             (ps)
           Unit for time values: fs, ps, ns, us, ms, s
 -[no]w                     (no)
           View output .xvg, .xpm, .eps and .pdb files
 -xvg    <enum>             (xmgrace)
           xvg plot formatting: xmgrace, xmgr, none
 -skip   <int>              (1)

           Change time step between input frames (ps)

           PBC treatment (see help text for full description): none, mol, res,
           atom, nojump, cluster, whole
 -ur     <enum>             (rect)
           Unit-cell representation: rect, tric, compact
 -[no]center                (no)
           Center atoms in box

        "esp": "Protein Data Bank file",
        "xtc": "Compressed trajectory file in XTC format",

        "tng": "Trajectory file in TNG format",

        "cpt": "Checkpoint file",

    # the first frame has been read; that is emulated below.

    fit_mode = state.value("fit") or "none"

    ref_file = state.file_value("s")

    masses = []

            err_write(PBC_WARNING)
    else:
        frames0 = _read_frames(traj_file)
        reference = frames0[0] if frames0 else None
        masses = [0.0] * (len(reference.atoms) if reference else 0)
    if state.is_set("n") and state.file_value("n") is not None:
        groups = parse_ndx(state.file_value("n"))
    else:

    def prompt_one(heading):
        out_write(heading + "\n")
        return prompt_groups_stderr(ctx, groups, 1)[0]

    fit_group = None

            raise GmxError(

                source="src/gromacs/gmxpreprocess/trjconv.cpp", line=1,
                function=None, module_stage=True)

    if state.value("center"):
        center_group = prompt_one("Select a group to be centered")
    cluster_group = None
    if (state.value("pbc") or "none") == "cluster":
        cluster_group = prompt_one("Select a group to be clustered")
    out_group = prompt_one("Select group for output")
    out_indices = list(out_group.indices)

    raw_frames = _read_frames(traj_file)

    begin = float(state.value("b")) * tfactor if state.is_set("b") else None
    end = float(state.value("e")) * tfactor if state.is_set("e") else None
    dt_opt = float(state.value("dt")) * tfactor if state.is_set("dt") else 0.0
    skip = int(state.value("skip") or 1)
    dump_time = float(state.value("dump")) * tfactor if state.is_set("dump") else -1.0
    pbc_mode = state.value("pbc") or "none"
    ur = state.value("ur") or "rect"
    boxcenter_mode = state.value("boxcenter") or "tric"
    trans = _vec3(state, "trans") if state.is_set("trans") else [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    shift = _vec3(state, "shift") if state.is_set("shift") else [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    drop_data = []
    if state.is_set("drop") and state.file_value("drop"):
        from .structures import read_lines
        for line in read_lines(state.file_value("drop")):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 2 and not line.startswith(("#", "@")):
                try:
                    drop_data.append((float(parts[0]), float(parts[1])))
                except ValueError:

                  f"{len(first.atoms)} atoms.\n")

    prev_fitted_ref = None
    analyzed = 0
    last_written = None

    first_time = raw_frames[0].time if raw_frames else 0.0

SYNOPSIS

gmx nonbonded-benchmark [-o [<.csv>]] [-size <int>] [-nt <int>]
             [-simd <enum>] [-coulomb <enum>] [-interactmodifier <enum>]
             [-[no]table] [-combrule <enum>] [-[no]halflj] [-[no]energy]
             [-[no]all] [-cutoff <real>] [-iter <int>] [-warmup <int>]
             [-[no]cycles] [-[no]time]

DESCRIPTION

gmx nonbonded-benchmark runs benchmarks for one or more so-called Nbnxm
non-bonded pair kernels. The non-bonded pair kernels are the most compute
intensive part of MD simulations and usually comprise 60 to 90 percent of the
runtime. For this reason they are highly optimized and several different
setups are available to compute the same physical interactions. In addition,
there are different physical treatments of Coulomb interactions and
optimizations for atoms without Lennard-Jones interactions. There are also
different physical treatments of Lennard-Jones interactions, but only a plain
cut-off is supported in this tool, as that is by far the most common
treatment. And finally, while force output is always necessary, energy output
is only required at certain steps. In total there are 36 relevant combinations
of options. The combinations double to 72 when two different SIMD setups are
supported. These combinations can be run with a single invocation using the
-all option. The behavior of each kernel is affected by caching behavior,
which is determined by the hardware used together with the system size and the
cut-off radius. The larger the number of atoms per thread, the more L1 cache
is needed to avoid L1 cache misses. The cut-off radius mainly affects the data
reuse: a larger cut-off results in more data reuse and makes the kernel less
sensitive to cache misses.

OpenMP parallelization is used to utilize multiple hardware threads within a
compute node. In these benchmarks there is no interaction between threads,
apart from starting and closing a single OpenMP parallel region per iteration.
Additionally, threads interact through sharing and evicting data from shared
caches. The number of threads to use is set with the -nt option. Thread
affinity is important, especially with SMT and shared caches. Affinities can
be set through the OpenMP library using the GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY environment
variable.

The benchmark tool times one or more kernels by running them repeatedly for a
number of iterations set by the -iter option. An initial kernel call is done
to avoid additional initial cache misses. Times are recording in cycles read
from efficient, high accuracy counters in the CPU. Note that these often do
not correspond to actual clock cycles. For each kernel, the tool reports the
total number of cycles, cycles per iteration, and (total and useful) pair
interactions per cycle. Because a cluster pair list is used instead of an atom
pair list, interactions are also computed for some atom pairs that are beyond
the cut-off distance. These pairs are not useful (except for additional
buffering, but that is not of interest here), only a side effect of the
cluster-pair setup. The SIMD 2xMM kernel has a higher useful pair ratio then
the 4xM kernel due to a smaller cluster size, but a lower total pair
throughput. It is best to run this, or for that matter any, benchmark with
locked CPU clocks, as thermal throttling can significantly affect performance.
If that is not an option, the -warmup option can be used to run initial,
untimed iterations to warm up the processor.

The most relevant regime is between 0.1 to 1 millisecond per iteration. Thus
it is useful to run with system sizes that cover both ends of this regime.

The -simd and -table options select different implementations to compute the
same physics. The choice of these options should ideally be optimized for the
target hardware. Historically, we only found tabulated Ewald correction to be
useful on 2-wide SIMD or 4-wide SIMD without FMA support. As all modern
architectures are wider and support FMA, we do not use tables by default. The
only exceptions are kernels without SIMD, which only support tables. Options
-coulomb, -combrule, -interactmodifier and -halflj depend on the force field
and composition of the simulated system. The optimization of computing
Lennard-Jones interactions for only half of the atoms in a cluster is useful
for water, which does not use Lennard-Jones on hydrogen atoms in most water
models. In the MD engine, any clusters where at most half of the atoms have LJ
interactions will automatically use this kernel. And finally, the -energy
option selects the computation of energies, which are usually only needed
infrequently.

OPTIONS

Options to specify output files:

 -o      [<.csv>]           (nonbonded-benchmark.csv) (Opt.)
           Also output results in csv format
</output>

{"command":"python3 - << 'PY'
p='app/gmxclone/tools.py';s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('def _nonbonded_benchmark')
new=r'''def _nonbonded_benchmark(ctx, state):
    import time as _time

    size_factor = int(state.value("size") or 1)
    if size_factor <= 0 or (size_factor & (size_factor - 1)) != 0:
        raise GmxError(
            "The size factor has to be a power of 2\n", title="Fatal error:",
            source="src/gromacs/nbnxm/benchmark/bench_system.cpp", line=99,
            function=None, module_stage=True)
    # Factor the size into x >= y >= z stackings (powers of two).
    exps = [0, 0, 0]
    e = size_factor.bit_length() - 1
    for i in range(e):
        exps[i % 3] += 1
    # Distribute so that x >= y >= z as in the reference.
    exps.sort(reverse=True)
    stack = [2 ** v for v in exps]
    natoms = 3000 * size_factor
    cutoff = float(state.value("cutoff"))
    nthread = int(state.value("nt") or 1)
    niter = int(state.value("iter") or 100)
    warmup = int(state.value("warmup") or 0)
    energy = bool(state.value("energy"))
    if size_factor > 1:
        out_write(f"Stacking a box of 3000 atoms {stack[0]} x {stack[1]} x "
                  f"{stack[2]} times\n")
    out_write(f"System size:          {natoms} atoms\n")
    from .numerics import fmt_g as _fg

    out_write(f"Cut-off radius:       {fmt_g(cutoff)} nm\n")
    out_write(f"Number of threads:    {nthread}\n")
    out_write(f"Number of iterations: {niter}\n")
    out_write(f"Compute energies:     {'yes' if energy else 'no'}\n")
    ewald_corr = "table" if state.value("table") else "analytical"
    out_write(f"Ewald excl. corr.:    {ewald_corr}\n")
    out_write("\n")
    simd = state.value("simd") or "auto"
    use_time = bool(state.value("time"))

SYNOPSIS

gmx trjcat [-f [<.xtc/.trr/...> [...]]] [-n [<.ndx>]] [-demux [<.xvg>]]
           [-o [<.xtc/.trr/...> [...]]] [-tu <enum>] [-xvg <enum>]
           [-b <time>] [-e <time>] [-dt <time>] [-[no]settime] [-[no]sort]
           [-[no]keeplast] [-[no]overwrite] [-[no]cat]

DESCRIPTION

gmx trjcat concatenates several input trajectory files in sorted order. In
case of double time frames the one in the later file is used. By specifying
-settime you will be asked for the start time of each file. The input files
are taken from the command line, such that a command like gmx trjcat -f *.trr
-o fixed.trr should do the trick. Using -cat, you can simply paste several
files together without removal of frames with identical time stamps.

One important option is inferred when the output file is amongst the input
files. In that case that particular file will be appended to which implies you
do not need to store double the amount of data. Obviously the file to append
to has to be the one with lowest starting time since one can only append at
the end of a file.

If the -demux option is given, the N trajectories that are read, are written

SYNOPSIS

gmx hbond [-f [<.xtc/.trr/...>]] [-s [<.tpr/.gro/...>]] [-n [<.ndx>]]
          [-o [<.ndx>]] [-num [<.xvg>]] [-dist [<.xvg>]] [-ang [<.xvg>]]
          [-dan [<.xvg>]] [-b <time>] [-e <time>] [-dt <time>] [-tu <enum>]
          [-fgroup <selection>] [-xvg <enum>] [-[no]rmpbc] [-[no]pbc]
          [-sf <file>] [-selrpos <enum>] [-seltype <enum>] [-r <selection>]
          [-t <selection>] [-[no]m] [-[no]pf] [-cutoff <real>] [-hbr <real>]
          [-hba <real>] [-de <string>] [-ae <string>]

DESCRIPTION

gmx hbond allows using geometric definition of hydrogen bonds to define them
throughout the structure.

-r specifies reference selection, relative to which the search for hydrogen
bonds in target selection will develop. Note that all atoms in reference and
target selections should be either absolutely identical or non-overlapping at
all. Accepts dynamic selection.

-t specifies target selection, relative to which the search for hydrogen bonds
in reference selection will develop. Note that all atoms in reference and
target selections should be either absolutely identical or non-overlapping at
all. Accepts dynamic selection.

-m forces to merge together information in output index file about hydrogen
bonds if they differ only in hydrogen indices. This also means that
information about hydrogen atoms in the hydrogen bonds would not be written in
output index file at all.

-pf forces to write hydrogen bonds for each frame separately instead of
writing hydrogen bonds for the whole system. Each information about hydrogen
bonds in new frame will be stored in its own section of the output index file.

-cutoff is a real value that defines distance from donor to acceptor (and vice
versa) that used in neighbor search. Minimum (and also recommended) value is
0.35.

-hbr Sets the cutoff that is used when calculating hydrogen bond distances.
Recommended value: 0.35.

-hba Sets the cutoff that is used when calculating hydrogen bond angles.
Recommended value: 30.

-de Specifies the atomic elements that will be selected from the topology to
check if a given element is a potential hydrogen bond donor.

-ae Specifies the atomic elements that will be selected from the topology to
check if a given element is a potential hydrogen bond acceptor.

-num allows you to get a plot of the number of hydrogen bonds as a function of
time at the output.

-dist allows you to get a plot of the distance distribution of all hydrogen
bonds at the output.

-ang allows you to get a plot of the angular distribution of all hydrogen
bonds at the output.

-dan allows you to get a plot of the number of analyzed donors and acceptors
for each frame at the output.

def _xpm_characters(n):
    chars = ("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
             "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
             "0123456789!@#$%^&*()-_=+{}[]|;:,.<>?/~`")
    if n <= len(chars):
        return [chars[i] for i in range(n)], 1
    # Two-character codes.
    codes = []
    for i in range(n):
        codes.append(chars[i // len(chars)] + chars[i % len(chars)])
    return codes, 2


def write_xpm(ctx, filename, matrix, *, title, legend, xlabel, ylabel,
              xaxis, yaxis, minv=None, maxv=None, nlevels=40):
    """Write a GROMACS-style XPM matrix (grayscale, white to black)."""
    nrows = len(matrix)
    ncols = len(matrix[0]) if nrows else 0
    flat = [v for row in matrix for v in row]
    if minv is None:
        minv = min(flat) if flat else 0.0
    if maxv is None:
        maxv = max(flat) if flat else 0.0
    codes, cpp = _xpm_characters(nlevels)
    lines = []
    lines.append("/* XPM */")
    lines.append("/* This file can be converted to EPS by the GROMACS program xpm2ps */")
    lines.append(f'/* title:   "{title}" */')
    lines.append(f'/* legend:  "{legend}" */')
    lines.append(f'/* x-label: "{xlabel}" */')
    lines.append(f'/* y-label: "{ylabel}" */')
    lines.append('/* type:    "Continuous" */')
    lines.append("static char *gromacs_xpm[] = {")
    lines.append(f'"{ncols} {nrows} {nlevels:4d} {cpp}",')
    span = (maxv - minv) / (nlevels - 1) if nlevels > 1 else 0.0
    for i in range(nlevels):
        level = minv + i * span
        gray = int(round(255 * (1 - i / (nlevels - 1)))) if nlevels > 1 else 0
        color = f"#{gray:02X}{gray:02X}{gray:02X}"
        from .numerics import fmt_g

        lines.append(f'"{codes[i]}  c {color} " /* "{fmt_g(level)}" */,')
    lines.append("/* x-axis: " + "".join(f" {fmt_g(v)}" for v in xaxis) + " */")
    lines.append("/* y-axis: " + "".join(f" {fmt_g(v)}" for v in yaxis) + " */")
    # XPM rows go from the largest y value to the smallest.
    for row in reversed(matrix):
        pixels = []
        for v in row:
            if maxv > minv:
                idx = int(round((v - minv) / (maxv - minv) * (nlevels - 1)))
            else:
                idx = 0
            idx = max(0, min(nlevels - 1, idx))
            pixels.append(codes[idx])
        lines.append(f'"{"".join(pixels)}",')
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    ctx.write_output_file(filename, text)
    return filename

    for i in range(n):

                for a in range(len(indices)):

                        d1 = math.sqrt(sum((frames[i][a][d] - frames[i][b][d]) ** 2
                                           for d in range(3)))
                        d2 = math.sqrt(sum((frames[j][a][d] - frames[j][b][d]) ** 2
                                           for d in range(3)))
                        ssum += (d1 - d2) ** 2; cnt += 1
                value = math.sqrt(ssum / cnt) if cnt else 0.0

            else:

            matrix[i][j] = value
            matrix[j][i] = value

    err_write("\n")
    flat = [matrix[i][j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j]
    rmsmin = min(flat) if flat else 0.0
    rmsmax = max(flat) if flat else 0.0
    avg = sum(flat) / len(flat) if flat else 0.0
    energy = sum(v * v for v in flat) / len(flat) if flat else 0.0
    # The reference's "energy of the matrix" is the mean square value
    # over the full matrix including the diagonal.
    energy = sum(matrix[i][j] ** 2 for i in range(n) for j in range(n)) / (n * n) if n else 0.0
    err_write(f"\nThe RMSD ranges from {fmt_g(f32(rmsmin))} to {fmt_g(f32(rmsmax))} nm\n")

    err_write(f"\nFound {len(clusters)} clusters\n\n")

    if state.is_set("sz"):

                  xlabel="Cluster #", ylabel="# Structures", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
                  extra_at=["@g0 type bar"] if False else None,
                  row_formatter=lambda r: f"{int(r[0]):8d}{int(r[1]):9d}")
    if state.is_set("clid"):
        clus_of = {}
        for ci, members in enumerate(clusters, 1):
            for m in members:
                clus_of[m] = ci
        rows = [[times[i], float(clus_of.get(i, 0))] for i in range(n)]
        write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("clid"), rows, title="Clusters",
                  xlabel="Time (ps)", ylabel="Cluster #", legends=[],
                  xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),

        ctx.write_output_file(state.file_value("clndx"), text)
    if state.is_set("cl"):

    if state.is_set("ev"):

def _cluster_frames(matrix, cutoff, method, state):
    n = len(matrix)
    if method == "gromos":
        remaining = set(range(n))
        clusters = []
        while remaining:
            best = None; best_neighbors = []
            for i in sorted(remaining):
                neigh = [j for j in remaining if matrix[i][j] <= cutoff]
                if len(neigh) > len(best_neighbors):
                    best, best_neighbors = i, neigh
            clusters.append(sorted(best_neighbors))
            remaining -= set(best_neighbors)
        return clusters
    if method == "jarvis-patrick":
        M = int(state.value("M") or 10)
        P = int(state.value("P") or 3)
        neighbors = []
        for i in range(n):
            ordered = sorted(range(n), key=lambda j: matrix[i][j])
            if M > 0:
                neighbors.append(set(ordered[:M]))
            else:
                neighbors.append({j for j in range(n) if matrix[i][j] <= cutoff})
        parent = list(range(n))

        def find(x):
            while parent[x] != x:
                parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; x = parent[x]
            return x

        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                if j in neighbors[i] and i in neighbors[j] and \
                        len(neighbors[i] & neighbors[j]) >= P:
                    parent[find(i)] = find(j)
        groups = {}
        for i in range(n):
            groups.setdefault(find(i), []).append(i)
        return list(groups.values())
    # Default: single linkage (also used as a fallback for the other
    # stochastic / spectral methods in this implementation).
    parent = list(range(n))

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; x = parent[x]
        return x

    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if matrix[i][j] <= cutoff:
                parent[find(i)] = find(j)
    groups = {}
    for i in range(n):
        groups.setdefault(find(i), []).append(i)
    return list(groups.values())


def _cluster_dist(ctx, state, flat, rmsmin, rmsmax):
    nbins = 100
    lo, hi = rmsmin, rmsmax
    bw = (hi - lo) / nbins if hi > lo else 1.0
    counts = [0] * nbins
    for v in flat:
        idx = int((v - lo) / bw) if bw else 0
        if 0 <= idx < nbins:
            counts[idx] += 1
    rows = [[lo + (i + 0.5) * bw, float(counts[i])] for i in range(nbins)]
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("dist"), rows, title="RMS Distribution",
              xlabel="RMS (nm)", ylabel="counts", legends=[],
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
              row_formatter=lambda r: f" {fmt_g(f32(r[0]))}  {fmt_g(f32(r[1]))}")


def _cluster_write_structures(ctx, state, runner, clusters, middle_info,
                              indices):
    from .structures import format_pdb, format_gro, format_g96, read_frames

    raw_frames = read_frames(state.file_value("f"))
    outfile = state.file_value("cl")
    ext = outfile.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in outfile else "pdb"
    if ext in ("xtc", "trr", "tng", "h5md", "cpt"):
        raise GmxError(
            "Writing binary trajectories is not supported by this "
            "reimplementation.\n", title="Fatal error:",
            source="src/gromacs/fileio/trxio.cpp", line=1, function=None)
    wcl = int(state.value("wcl") or 0)
    nst = int(state.value("nst") or 1)
    frames_out = []
    for ci, members in enumerate(clusters):
        if wcl and ci >= wcl:
            break
        if len(members) < nst:
            continue
        if state.value("av"):
            # Average structure of the cluster.
            avg = runner.reference.copy()
            for a in avg.atoms:
                a.pos = tuple(
                    sum(raw_frames[m].atoms[avg.atoms.index(a)].pos[d]
                        for m in members) / len(members) for d in range(3)) \
                    if False else a.pos
            # Simpler: average by atom position in the frame list.
            for ai, a in enumerate(avg.atoms):
                a.pos = tuple(
                    sum(raw_frames[m].atoms[ai].pos[d] for m in members)
                    / len(members) for d in range(3))
            frames_out.append(avg)
        else:
            middle = middle_info[ci][0] if ci < len(middle_info) else members[0]
            frames_out.append(raw_frames[middle])
    if ext == "gro":
        text = "".join(format_gro(f) for f in frames_out)
    elif ext == "g96":
        text = "".join(format_g96(f) for f in frames_out)
    else:
        text = ""
        for mi, f in enumerate(frames_out, 1):
            txt = format_pdb(f)
            txt = txt.replace("MODEL        1", f"MODEL        {mi}")
            text += txt
    ctx.write_output_file(outfile, text)


def _cluster_eigen(ctx, state, matrix, times):
    from .fitting import _jacobi_eigen

    n = len(matrix)
    if n == 0:
        return
    vals, vecs = _jacobi_eigen(matrix)
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: -vals[i])
    rows = [[float(i + 1), vals[order[i]]] for i in range(n)]
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("ev"), rows,
              title="Eigenvalues of the RMSD matrix", xlabel="Eigenvalue index",
              ylabel="Eigenvalue", legends=[], xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
              row_formatter=lambda r: f" {fmt_g(r[0])}  {fmt_g(r[1])}")


def _cluster_transitions(ctx, state, clusters, times, nlevels):
    from .fileio import write_xpm

    n = len(times)
    clus_of = {}
    for ci, members in enumerate(clusters):
        for m in members:
            clus_of[m] = ci
    k = len(clusters)
    trans = [[0] * k for _ in range(k)]
    seq = [clus_of.get(i, -1) for i in range(n)]
    total = 0
    for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
        if a >= 0 and b >= 0 and a != b:
            trans[a][b] += 1

def _cluster_frames(matrix, cutoff, method, state):
    n = len(matrix)
    if method == "gromos":
        remaining = set(range(n))
        clusters = []
        while remaining:
            best = None; best_neighbors = []
            for i in sorted(remaining):
                neigh = [j for j in remaining if matrix[i][j] <= cutoff]
                if len(neigh) > len(best_neighbors):
                    best, best_neighbors = i, neigh
            clusters.append(sorted(best_neighbors))
            remaining -= set(best_neighbors)
        return clusters
    if method == "jarvis-patrick":
        M = int(state.value("M") or 10)
        P = int(state.value("P") or 3)
        neighbors = []
        for i in range(n):
            ordered = sorted(range(n), key=lambda j: matrix[i][j])
            if M > 0:
                neighbors.append(set(ordered[:M]))
            else:
                neighbors.append({j for j in range(n) if matrix[i][j] <= cutoff})
        parent = list(range(n))

        def find(x):
            while parent[x] != x:
                parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; x = parent[x]
            return x

        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                if j in neighbors[i] and i in neighbors[j] and \
                        len(neighbors[i] & neighbors[j]) >= P:
                    parent[find(i)] = find(j)
        groups = {}
        for i in range(n):
            groups.setdefault(find(i), []).append(i)
        return list(groups.values())
    # Default: single linkage (also used as a fallback for the other
    # stochastic / spectral methods in this implementation).
    parent = list(range(n))

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]; x = parent[x]
        return x

    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if matrix[i][j] <= cutoff:
                parent[find(i)] = find(j)
    groups = {}
    for i in range(n):
        groups.setdefault(find(i), []).append(i)
    return list(groups.values())


def _cluster_dist(ctx, state, flat, rmsmin, rmsmax):
    nbins = 100
    lo, hi = rmsmin, rmsmax
    bw = (hi - lo) / nbins if hi > lo else 1.0
    counts = [0] * nbins
    for v in flat:
        idx = int((v - lo) / bw) if bw else 0
        if 0 <= idx < nbins:
            counts[idx] += 1
    rows = [[lo + (i + 0.5) * bw, float(counts[i])] for i in range(nbins)]
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("dist"), rows, title="RMS Distribution",
              xlabel="RMS (nm)", ylabel="counts", legends=[],
              xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
              row_formatter=lambda r: f" {fmt_g(f32(r[0]))}  {fmt_g(f32(r[1]))}")


def _cluster_write_structures(ctx, state, runner, clusters, middle_info,
                              indices):
    from .structures import format_pdb, format_gro, format_g96, read_frames

    raw_frames = read_frames(state.file_value("f"))
    outfile = state.file_value("cl")
    ext = outfile.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in outfile else "pdb"
    if ext in ("xtc", "trr", "tng", "h5md", "cpt"):
        raise GmxError(
            "Writing binary trajectories is not supported by this "
            "reimplementation.\n", title="Fatal error:",
            source="src/gromacs/fileio/trxio.cpp", line=1, function=None)
    wcl = int(state.value("wcl") or 0)
    nst = int(state.value("nst") or 1)
    frames_out = []
    for ci, members in enumerate(clusters):
        if wcl and ci >= wcl:
            break
        if len(members) < nst:
            continue
        if state.value("av"):
            # Average structure of the cluster.
            avg = runner.reference.copy()
            for a in avg.atoms:
                a.pos = tuple(
                    sum(raw_frames[m].atoms[avg.atoms.index(a)].pos[d]
                        for m in members) / len(members) for d in range(3)) \
                    if False else a.pos
            # Simpler: average by atom position in the frame list.
            for ai, a in enumerate(avg.atoms):
                a.pos = tuple(
                    sum(raw_frames[m].atoms[ai].pos[d] for m in members)
                    / len(members) for d in range(3))
            frames_out.append(avg)
        else:
            middle = middle_info[ci][0] if ci < len(middle_info) else members[0]
            frames_out.append(raw_frames[middle])
    if ext == "gro":
        text = "".join(format_gro(f) for f in frames_out)
    elif ext == "g96":
        text = "".join(format_g96(f) for f in frames_out)
    else:
        text = ""
        for mi, f in enumerate(frames_out, 1):
            txt = format_pdb(f)
            txt = txt.replace("MODEL        1", f"MODEL        {mi}")
            text += txt
    ctx.write_output_file(outfile, text)


def _cluster_eigen(ctx, state, matrix, times):
    from .fitting import _jacobi_eigen

    n = len(matrix)
    if n == 0:
        return
    vals, vecs = _jacobi_eigen(matrix)
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: -vals[i])
    rows = [[float(i + 1), vals[order[i]]] for i in range(n)]
    write_xvg(ctx, state.file_value("ev"), rows,
              title="Eigenvalues of the RMSD matrix", xlabel="Eigenvalue index",
              ylabel="Eigenvalue", legends=[], xvg_format=state.value("xvg"),
              row_formatter=lambda r: f" {fmt_g(r[0])}  {fmt_g(r[1])}")


def _cluster_transitions(ctx, state, clusters, times, nlevels):
    from .fileio import write_xpm

    n = len(times)
    clus_of = {}
    for ci, members in enumerate(clusters):
        for m in members:
            clus_of[m] = ci
    k = len(clusters)
    trans = [[0] * k for _ in range(k)]
    seq = [clus_of.get(i, -1) for i in range(n)]
    total = 0
    for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
        if a >= 0 and b >= 0 and a != b:
            trans[a][b] += 1
            total += 1
    err_write(f"Counted {total} transitions in total, max "
              f"{max([max(r) for r in trans], default=0)} between two "

    if state.is_set("tr"):
        maxv = max([max(r) for r in trans], default=0)
        if maxv <= 0:
